In the row the library's name stands as a link after `Chart:`, the way the sources stand after `Data:`. The full form follows: the three sources, the privacy sentence, the maker, then "Sky chart: glyphcss." as its sixth line, so the sources and the page's own lines keep the order every earlier capture shows and the fourth credit is what was added, in each form, at the end. *(V22-15)* As first built the item carried a second name after a comma and the sentence a second link; the third session took both out, and the order above is the one that stayed.
- **D-664 — The one-row footer wraps under 1118 px (en) and 1137 px (es); the 1280 px captures hold one line.** (R102; FR-SHOW-8, D-657; **amended V22-15**.) Measured on the built app by a one-off Playwright script (`sdd-run/`, not kept), with the library alone in the row: the wide row holds one line from 1118 px of viewport in English and 1137 px in Spanish, and is two lines from `WIDE_MIN_PX` (964) up to those widths, the 1024 px capture width among them and the 1280 one not. With the author's name in the row the same script had found 1330/1349, so the wrap that reached every desk capture width then reaches only the mid width now, and the 1280 × 800 desk keeps the shell height every earlier requirement was measured against. FR-SHOW-8 allows the one wrap and D-657 pins no literal for the gate; the pair is `FOOTER_ONE_LINE_MIN_PX` because D-681 needs it (D-666). At 1920 the content is capped at `HOME_MAX_CELLS` (FR-HOME-4) and the row holds one line. What the wrap costs under the fold is one row of the D-119 shell's height — paid from the shell's air, not the panes, by D-681's rule (D-666); `desktop.spec.ts`'s bottom-of-screen and one-`<p>` assertions hold as written. The English fold equals `HOME_THREE_PANE_MIN_PX` (1118) by measurement, not by construction: FR-HOME-3's 1118 × 700 check therefore runs with a one-line footer in English and a two-line one in Spanish, and is green in both.
- **D-665 — `LinkedText` stays a one-link sentence; the catalog test reads the short row and the library's name.** (R102; D-657; **amended V22-15**.) The first two sessions gave the interface optional `middle` and `link2` fields for a second link, rendered only together; V22-15 took the second link out and with it the fields, so `LinkedText` is the shape it was and `Linked` renders one anchor. What stays from that work: `messages.test.ts` renders `footer.chart` with the other linked sentences and the short row's four strings (`footer.short` was not rendered before), so the Spanish and never-address-the-reader checks cover them; `glyphcss` and `(CC BY 4.0)` join the shared set as names (FR-I18N-6). `git grep -i fortunatti src tests` finds one line on the branch, `tests/docs/public.test.ts`'s README pin, which is `main`'s and P3's to remove with the README paragraph (FR-PUB-4 as amended).
- **D-666 — The shell's air is one calculation, and the two rules that take from it are shares of a row.** (R102 resumed; FR-HOME-3 as amended, FR-SHOW-8; D-681, D-608, D-664; **amended V22-15**.) D-681 asks for two rules that compose — the short window's (D-608) and the two-line footer's — with both true leaving no padding above or below the panes. Two media blocks each writing `calc(var(--row) / 2)` would not compose: whichever wins the cascade leaves half. So the wide `.main` rule (`App.module.css`) owns the padding once, `calc(var(--row) * (1 - var(--short-window) - var(--two-line-footer)))`, and each rule sets its own custom property to `0.5` — a number, the share of the row it takes, so the wide blocks keep to cells and rows (FR-DESK-1's test) — and under 720 px tall below the literal the two shares are the whole row. `FOOTER_ONE_LINE_MIN_PX = { en: 1118, es: 1137 }` in `lib/layout.ts` is D-664's measurement and nothing derives it; the stylesheet writes it as `(min-width: 964px) and (width < 1118px)` under `:root[lang='en']` and `(width < 1137px)` under `es`, the header's fold syntax (D-546), so the literal appears verbatim and the block still counts as a wide one. The footer's half is on `#root > footer[data-form='short']` from the same block: the settings page's own foot (FR-SET-1) is not that element and keeps its padding, and the line form (D-548) is compact-only and never under the query. `breakpoint.test.ts` holds the pair, its order (Spanish the longer), its place between the 1024 and 1280 px capture widths and under the split literal, and each block's two rules and nothing else. `home-desk.spec.ts` is unchanged but for a comment naming D-681: FR-HOME-2 at 1024 × 768 and FR-HOME-3 at 1118 × 700 are green in both languages with no number moved. The captures: the row's text changes in every file whose footer is in the picture, so the five footer screens were re-shot whole (V22-15); against `main` the 1024 px files show the fourth credit on a second line with half a row less air above and below the panes, and every other width shows the fourth credit on the one line and the shell as it was. The one-off measurement script and the `CAPTURES=1` wrapper config live under `sdd-run/` (ignored) and are not committed.
- **D-671 — The `promo` project is in the config only when the command line asked for it.** (P4; FR-SHOW-6, D-652.) A bare `playwright test` — `npm run e2e`, CI — runs every project in the config, so a `promo` project that was always listed would have recorded under both whatever the other three ignore. `playwright.config.ts` exports `promoSelected(argv)` (`--project=promo` or `--project promo`) and adds `PROMO_PROJECT` to `projects` only when it is true; because every worker loads the config again with its own argv, the runner's answer is relayed as `PLAYWRIGHT_PROMO=1` in the environment the workers inherit ("Project not found in the worker process" otherwise). `tests/docs/promo.test.ts` asserts both spellings select it, that the process running vitest sees no such project, and that the three other projects ignore the file; `npx playwright test --list` shows none of its eight tests and `--project=promo --list` shows all of them. The project keeps `fullyParallel: false`, `retries: 0` and a 180 s timeout: a recording wants the box to itself, a second take is the same file written twice, and `afterAll` in the one worker moves every video the file produced.
- **D-672 — One context per flow, recording at its device's frame.** (P4; FR-SHOW-6, D-652.) Two frames in one file is more than `test.use` allows: Playwright refuses a `video` option inside a `describe` ("it forces a new worker"), and at file level it is one size for every test. So `promo-record.spec.ts` opens `browser.newContext` per flow with the device's viewport, pixel ratio, touch and `recordVideo: { dir, size }` — `tests/e2e/promoFlows.ts`'s `DEVICES`: the phone 390 × 844 at 3× asking for 1170 × 2532, the desk 1440 × 900 asking for its own size — and closes it in `done`, which is what finishes the file; `afterAll` moves the closed files. The project's own `video` option stays as D-652 wrote it, the phone frame, for any page the fixture would open. The frame the first run produced is what was asked, 1170 × 2532 (VP8, 25 fps; Chromium's screencast did not cap it), and the desk 1440 × 900. The `.mp4` is D-652's `libx264` and `yuv420p` plus `-vf scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2`, which keeps the even dimensions the encoder wants whatever frame a screencast produces, and `-movflags +faststart` for a file a feed streams; `ffmpeg` is found by scanning `PATH` for the executable, the way a shell resolves it, and one line per file says which of the two was written.
- **D-673 — The flows are seeded from two modules, every flow on the capture set's night, and the phone's live flow is that night by day.** (P4; FR-SHOW-6, D-653, D-654, D-179.) The capture spec exported nothing, so its night, its seed and its two waits — `CLOCK`, `GLARE_PASS`, `SHOWN`, `TICK_MS`, `seedPrefs`, `seedPage`, `stubNetwork`, `guide`, `listSettled`, `pinnedAt` — moved whole to `tests/e2e/captureSeeds.ts`, which `v1-captures.spec.ts` imports (its routes stay where they were; `ci.test.ts`'s F-48 check reads the helper there). The list — name, device, language, theme, seconds, stills — is `tests/e2e/promoFlows.ts`, the `captureSet.ts` shape, because a Playwright spec cannot be imported by a unit test (`test()` at module load) and the config wants the phone frame; the spec re-exports `PROMO_FLOWS` from it. **Every flow runs over Paris on the capture set's night**, not the lists at Neuquén nine days on as FR-SHOW-6's text has it: nine days on the elements are past FR-SAT-4's five-day threshold, so the home of the three first runs, the list, the settings and the desk's cold open carried the amber `Elements 9 d 4 h old` line — a warning a reader of a fresh install never sees, and promo material must not show one — which is the reason D-179 moved the capture set to Paris. So `scripts/build-stored-run.ts` writes a second fixture, `tests/fixtures/stored-run-paris.json`, the same 72 h search over Paris at `CLOCK` (`observers.ts`'s `PARIS_NIGHT`, 2026-09-02 03:00 UTC, where the elements are seven hours old and the ISS rises at 03:52, fifty minutes ahead, so the countdown runs on camera); `stored-run-neuquen.json` is written as before, byte for byte, and the rest of the suite does not move. The list flows seed that run into IndexedDB before the place is typed (the R82 method) and type Paris's coordinates, so the panes fill on the tap and the recompute runs on camera behind them; what the seed shows instead of the warning is the capture set's cost, a cloud badge reading `Weather unknown` and the readiness line's "no cloud forecast stored yet", because the only recorded forecast is over Neuquén (D-179). `tests/docs/promo.test.ts` holds the Paris run to `PARIS` at `PARIS_NIGHT` with its elements under `EPOCH_WARN_MS`, and the spec to that run and that clock, never `NINE_DAYS_ON`. The charts run over the same Paris: the desk's live flow at `SHOWN`, the ISS overhead; the phone's at `CLOCK + 12 h` (15:00 UTC), because `[ see this pass ]` is offered only while nothing is up and the next rise is between two minutes and a day ahead (FR-JUMP-1), and three minutes into the overhead pass it is not there — by day the headline counts to the evening's first rise and the one tap holds the page there with its arc drawn. Between actions the paused clock is run forward by `watch`: 50 ms of `runFor` then 50 ms of wall time, twenty times a second, so the countdown ticks and the bead moves in the file at the reader's pace while every instant on screen is still the fixture's. The flows' `seconds` are the watching stretches (12–18 s); the files came out at 17–29 s including the loads, under FR-SHOW-6's 40. `afterAll` converts each video on its own: an `ffmpeg` that exits non-zero is caught, named in one printed line, and the loop goes on, so a failed conversion costs that flow its `.mp4` (its `.webm` is already in `promo/media/`) and nothing of the flows after it, where one throw would have left their videos in `test-results/` for the next run to wipe.
- **D-675 — `knip.json` as filled: `ffmpeg` ignored as a binary, `docs/**` not ignored.** (P5; FR-SHOW-4, D-647.) Two things the decision's text did not foresee, both from running knip 6.38 (what the precondition's `npm install` resolved; the audit's 5.x reported 83 exports and 39 types, this version 172 and 58 under the same rule, so the counts in FR-SHOW-4 are the audit's and the task's `Done` note carries the run's). First, knip reads `execFileSync('ffmpeg', …)` in `tests/e2e/promo-record.spec.ts` as an unlisted binary; `ffmpeg` is the optional system converter D-652 and D-672 describe, found on `PATH` and never a dependency, so `ignoreBinaries: ["ffmpeg"]` is the one entry beside the empty `ignoreDependencies` — a binary is not a dependency, and D-647's rule for the latter (removed, or the reason written beside it) is kept by writing the reason here. Second, knip prints a configuration hint on every run for an `ignore` pattern no analysed file matches, and `docs/**` is captures and data with no source under it; a report that prints a line is not the empty report the task is measured by, so `ignore` is `spike/**` alone and the result is what D-647 wanted, `docs/**` contributing nothing to the analysis either way. `entry` is `scripts/*.ts` and `spike/**/main.tsx` as written; Vite, Vitest and Playwright's entries come from their plugins.
- **D-676 — A duplicate's alias loses its keyword, and the test that imported the alias imports the kept name.** (P5; FR-SHOW-4, D-648.) Two of the four duplicates resolved themselves — `KEY_STEP_MS` and `EXTENT_TOP_UNITS` were on the unused list and lost their keyword by the rule. The other two aliases were each imported by one test: `LIVE_FOLD_ACTIONS_UNDER_PX` (`foldRows.test.ts`) and `INK_HEIGHT_UNITS` (`camera.test.ts`). D-648 names `TAP_PX` and §12 names `DRAWING_HEIGHT_UNITS` for FR-DOME-1, so those are the kept names; each alias stays as a local `const` its file reads, and the two tests import the kept name in its place, the assertions unchanged (the values are equal by definition). This is the one hunk shape beyond D-648's three — an import specifier renamed in a test — and it is the smallest edit that leaves one export per value; no test was changed to pass, and none was deleted, because nothing on knip's list had a test importing it.

- **D-667 — *By the numbers* is read at the `main` commit the task branched from, not at the task's own.** (P3; FR-SHOW-1, FR-SHOW-2, D-650.) A figure needs a commit a reader can check out. The task's commits are squashed at merge, so a branch SHA in the table would name a commit `main` never has; the base commit (`2b6ff66` for P3) is on `main` for good. The cost is stated in the table's preamble: the task's own edits move the three documents' line counts by a few lines and add one test file, and the figures are the base's. The `npm test` row is measured, not derived: the session swapped the base commit's `tests/docs` files back in and ran the suite once (2165 tests in 194 files, against the branch's 2213 in 195), so the row is what the command printed at the tree it names. A later phase that rewrites the page re-reads every row at its own base and changes the one SHA.
- **D-668 — `docs/RELEASE.md` keeps every released version's checklist as history, marked, and only its current sections are read for paths.** (P3; FR-SHOW-1.) §6 to §13 are the lists of releases that happened and name files, budgets and sentences as they stood then — `FollowPhone.tsx`, main at 155 — and rewriting them would falsify the record the way editing a Done note would. Each carries a one-line `> *History (…)*` marker under its heading; `accuracy.test.ts` asserts the marker sits on exactly §6–§9 and §11–§13 and drops those sections before scanning the file for paths and scripts, while the stale-string check reads the whole file. §1–§5, §10 and the last section are current and are held to the tree. The intro says the same in words: §14 is the phase in progress, §13 the last release.
- **D-669 — What counts as a path claim.** (P3; D-650.) A backticked token with a `/` under `docs`, `scripts`, `src`, `tests`, `public`, `spike`, `.claude` or `.github` must be a tracked file or a directory holding one; a bare token with a file extension must be the basename of a tracked file, so the README's `catalog.json` and a skill's `Footer.tsx` pass without a path and a `no-such.ts` fails. Anything with a glob, a placeholder, a `$`, whitespace or a leading `/` is not a claim (`docs/screenshots/v1-*.png`, `sdd-run/<id>.brief.md`, `/third-party-notices.txt`). A document with no claims would pass vacuously, so the test also asserts the rule found more than forty across the set. The same reading covers `npm run <x>` against `package.json`'s scripts and `npx tsx scripts/<x>.ts` against the tree. The visual-review skill's example names were the first thing the rule caught: `r16-home-1280.png` and two more named captures that never existed, replaced with real files.

### 2.37 v2.2.1 decisions (2026-09-28)

The phase changes nothing the app does. Its decisions are where the showcase night lives in the tests, how the recordings and the captures reach it, and what the two new fixtures are. The instants below were computed with the app's own worker handler (`worker/handlers.ts`, the path `scripts/build-stored-run.ts` takes) over the committed 2026-09-02 elements; the tasks recompute them from the stored run and record any difference in their `Done` notes.

- **D-682 — The showcase night is constants in `observers.ts` and one option on `stubNetwork`.** (FR-SHOW-9; V22-16, V22-17.) `tests/e2e/observers.ts` is the Playwright-free module the stored-run script and the docs tests already read, so the night goes there beside `NEUQUEN` and `PARIS`: `BARILOCHE_QUERY = 'bariloche'`; `BARILOCHE`, the `Observer` the place picker would write — the first `Place` of `parseGeocodeBody` (`data/openMeteo/geocode.ts`) over the geocode fixture, passed to `lib/place.ts`'s `observerFromPlace` as `PlacePicker.tsx` does, so the name, the region, the altitude (839 m) and the zone (`America/Argentina/Salta`) are the app's and not typed by hand (F-49's rule, which R37 applied to coordinates); `SHOWCASE_NIGHT = Date.parse('2026-09-06T07:00:00Z')`, 04:00 local, 43 minutes before the night's first pass (04:43) and 1 h 48 min before its first bright one (Tiangong, 05:48); `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`, the instant FR-SAT-4's warning would appear — the fixtures' newest epoch (`2026-09-01T23:20:48Z`, read by `lib/elementsAge.ts`'s `newestEpoch`) plus `EPOCH_WARN_MS`, `2026-09-06T23:20:48Z`, 20:20 local — as a literal the test checks against the computation; `STORED_RUN_BARILOCHE_FILE`. `liveHelpers.ts`'s `stubNetwork(page, elements)` gains a third parameter, `weather: 'refused' | 'showcase' = 'refused'`: refused is today's behaviour for every existing caller, byte for byte; showcase fulfils `api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast` with the forecast fixture when the request's `latitude`/`longitude` are the fixture's cell (`-41.1`, `-71.3`) and refuses any other cell, and fulfils `geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search` with the geocode fixture when `name` is `bariloche` and refuses any other name, so a flow that drifts to another place fails loudly rather than showing Bariloche's weather over it.
- **D-683 — The recordings type the name and pick it, over a stored run at 04:00.** (P7; FR-SHOW-6 as amended, FR-SHOW-9; supersedes D-673's Paris run.) `scripts/build-stored-run.ts` writes `tests/fixtures/stored-run-bariloche.json`, the 72 h search over `BARILOCHE` at `SHOWCASE_NIGHT`, by the same `build()`; `stored-run-paris.json` and `STORED_RUN_PARIS_FILE` are deleted, since only the recordings read them, and `stored-run-neuquen.json` is written byte for byte as before. Every flow calls `stubNetwork(page, 'fixtures', 'showcase')` and seeds that run before the place is set (the R82 method, as D-673). The first-run and desk cold-open flows type `bariloche` into the place search, wait for the result list and pick the first result — the search is on camera and the observer is the picker's; the flows that open on a saved place seed `BARILOCHE` in `wiys:prefs:v1` as `seedPrefs` does today. The desk's live flow is at the showcase's `SHOWN`: three minutes into the night's brightest pass, Tiangong's rising at 07:20 local (peak −2.1, 48°, in twilight), read from the stored run by its object and start rather than written as a number. The phone's live flow stays "that night by day" for D-673's reason (`[ see this pass ]` is offered only while nothing is up): `SHOWCASE_NIGHT + 12 h`, 16:00 local on the 6th, under `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`. No flow runs its clock past `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`; `promo.test.ts` asserts each flow's start plus its seconds is under it. `captureSeeds.ts`, `v1-captures.spec.ts` and `captureSet.ts` are not touched by P7: the release set stays on Paris until P8 re-shoots it, so for one task the two nights differ, and FR-SHOW-9's "no seed module exports a Paris night for the capture set" is P8's to meet.
- **D-684 — The capture set moves onto the same seeds, its routes and its shape unchanged.** (P8; FR-SHOW-10, FR-SHOW-9, FR-CAP-1..5; supersedes D-179's "one place and one night: Paris" and D-639's instants.) `captureSeeds.ts`'s `CLOCK` becomes `SHOWCASE_NIGHT`, `SHOWN` the showcase's (D-683), and `seedPage`'s observer `BARILOCHE`; `v1-captures.spec.ts` calls `stubNetwork(page, 'fixtures', 'showcase')`. `GLARE_PASS` is re-derived: the capture run looks in the stored run for a pass the app flags with Moon glare on the night (the Moon is a 27 % waning crescent, 3–14° up in the north-east during the morning passes); if there is one it takes its place, and if there is none the screens that used it are shot on the night's brightest pass and their `what` lines say the glare state is absent and why (FR-SHOW-9's rule), the file names unchanged. The same for the `Next ISS` tag and any other state the night lacks. D-179's reason for closing the night groups on the home capture (fifty passes a night over Paris) is re-checked against Bariloche's count; the route stays as it is unless the count makes a capture unreviewable, and the `Done` note says which. `PARIS_NIGHT` leaves `observers.ts` when nothing imports it (knip's rule, D-648); `PARIS` stays for the specs that name it for their own reasons. `scripts/readme-hero.ts` is run as it is and the two pictures it writes are committed; the owner uploads `docs/readme/social-preview.png` again (FR-PUB-11). The two-run comparison of FR-CAP-5 is `captures.yml` twice on the branch's head, both run links in the pull request.
- **D-685 — The seeds' test reads the fixtures, not the specs' prose.** (FR-SHOW-9, FR-SHOW-10.) `tests/docs/showcase.test.ts`, created by P7 and extended by P8, imports `observers.ts` and the fixtures only (no Playwright): `BARILOCHE` deep-equals `observerFromPlace(parseGeocodeBody(fixture)[0])`; `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` and every instant `promoFlows.ts` names (and, from P8, `captureSeeds.ts`'s `CLOCK` and `SHOWN`) fall on 2026-09-05 or 2026-09-06 in `America/Argentina/Salta` and before `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`; `SHOWCASE_UNTIL` equals the newest epoch of the catalog-filtered fixture elements plus `EPOCH_WARN_MS`; the forecast fixture's cell is `BARILOCHE`'s by `passCellKey`'s rounding (D-37), its `hourly.time` covers every such instant, and none of its four series has a null; the stored Bariloche run's `observer` is `BARILOCHE` and its `computedAt` is `SHOWCASE_NIGHT`. From P8 it also asserts that `captureSeeds.ts` does not import `PARIS` or `PARIS_NIGHT`. `promo.test.ts`'s D-673 check (the Paris run at `PARIS_NIGHT`, never `NINE_DAYS_ON`) is rewritten to the Bariloche run at `SHOWCASE_NIGHT`.
- **D-686 — The two fixtures, and the one word on the forecast's `.meta.json`.** (FR-SHOW-9; V22-17.) `tests/fixtures/open-meteo/2026-09-06-bariloche-forecast.json` is the verbatim body of `https://historical-forecast-api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=-41.1&longitude=-71.3&hourly=cloud_cover,cloud_cover_low,cloud_cover_mid,cloud_cover_high&start_date=2026-09-06&end_date=2026-09-08&timezone=auto&timeformat=unixtime`, re-indented, captured 2026-09-28 with an `Origin` header (the response carried `access-control-allow-origin: *`): 72 hourly samples from `1788663600` (2026-09-06 00:00 local) to `1788919200`, four series, no nulls, `timezone: America/Argentina/Salta`, the model grid point `-41.019333, -71.25534`. Its `.meta.json` has the Neuquén fixture's fields (`fetchedAt`, `source`, `cell`, `observer`, `timezone`, `coverage`, `note`) and one more, `"kind": "historical-forecast reconstruction"`, and its `note` says in a sentence that the body was assembled after the fact from archived model runs and is not a forecast fetched at the clock, so the fixture's kind is a field a test can read and not a sentence a reader must find. `2026-09-06-bariloche-geocode.json` is the verbatim body of `https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search?name=bariloche&count=8&language=en&format=json` captured the same day, four results, the first `Bariloche, Rio Negro, Argentina` at `-41.14557, -71.30822`, 839 m; its `.meta.json` is the Cipolletti fixture's shape. Both files are named for the night they serve, not the day they were fetched, as the Neuquén forecast is. They are the owner's commit on `main` (V22-17), made from this session's captures.
- **D-687 — Each flow names its instant, and the recordings seed themselves.** (P7; FR-SHOW-9, D-683, D-685.) `PromoFlow` gains `at`, the instant its paused clock is installed at, so the docs tests read every instant a recording starts from the list rather than from the spec's prose: `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` for the first runs, the list, the settings and the desk's cold open; `SHOWCASE_BY_DAY` (`SHOWCASE_NIGHT + 12 h`) for the phone's live flow; `SHOWCASE_SHOWN` for the desk's. `promoFlows.ts` finds `BRIGHTEST_PASS` in the stored run as Tiangong (NORAD 48274) rising within the 07:20 local minute on the 6th, and `SHOWCASE_SHOWN` is its start plus three minutes; `showcase.test.ts` checks that it is the lowest peak magnitude before `SHOWCASE_UNTIL` (−2.14). `promo-record.spec.ts` seeds with its own `seedShowcase` (the prefs init script, `stubNetwork(page, 'fixtures', 'showcase')`, the clock at `of.at`) rather than `captureSeeds.seedPage`, whose private network stub refuses the forecast and which P7 may not touch; it still takes `guide`, `OPEN_GUIDE` and `SeedPrefs` from there. `SHOWCASE_UNTIL` is the literal D-682 names, `2026-09-06T23:20:48Z`; the newest epoch is `23:20:48.008Z`, so the test holds the literal to the computation floored to the second, and to the warning's own measure (`epochIsOld` false at it, true a second after). The forecast cell is checked with `weatherCache.cellCentre`, the 0.1° rounding D-37 means; `passCellKey`, which D-685 names, rounds to 0.01° and gives the stored run's key, not the forecast's.
- **D-688 — A picked place moves the first run on by itself, and the pointer leaves the page.** (P7; FR-FIRST-2, D-683.) A place picked from the list is settled (`useSteps` goes to `when` at once for any observer that is not a typed pair), so the first run has no `[ continue ]` to tap; the `where` still is shot with the recorded answer listed under `bariloche`, the search on screen, and the desk's `cold-open` still before typing, as before. After the pick the pointer is moved to the corner: the tap lands where the when step puts its sky box, and with a forecast that box has a tooltip, which in Spanish covered `[ Ver qué cruza ]` and failed the first take. The two live flows wait on `homeSettled` — a card, nothing busy, the night groups and the readiness line — because `captureSeeds.listSettled` also waits for the ISS's `Next` tag, which the night does not hold (FR-SHOW-9).
- **D-689 — What the first Bariloche run showed.** (P7; FR-SHOW-9.) All eight flows pass in 3.3 min; the countdown's first pass is Cosmos 2428 at 04:43 (`in 43:22` on the list still), the list and the desk's panes read `Clear` on every morning card and `Clouds now Clear`, the readiness line `Ready offline until 2026-09-08 22:09`, the Where reading `Elements 4 d 7 h old` without the warning, and the desk's live page, three minutes into Tiangong's 07:20 pass, `Partly cloudy, 31 % cloud`. Both live flows' held instants land on the evening's first rise, SL-16 R/B (Cosmos 2369) at 20:44 local, 24 minutes past `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`: the phone's `[ see this pass ]` from 16:00 and the desk's `[ pass ▶| ]` from 07:26 have nothing nearer to go to. No warning shows, because FR-SAT-4's warning reads the page's clock, which stays under `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`; whether FR-SHOW-9's "nothing after it is shown" also covers a held instant is the owner's to say (the phone's flow at `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` would hold at 04:43 instead). *(Superseded by D-690: it does, and neither flow holds the evening now.)*
- **D-690 — At the gate: 05:00, a morning hold, and the pass as a literal.** (P7; FR-SHOW-9 (a), FR-SHOW-6; the owner on PR #167, amends D-682's `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` and D-683's phone instant.) Three answers, one per question the first run left. **The clock starts at 05:00 local** (`SHOWCASE_NIGHT = 2026-09-06T08:00:00Z`, was 07:00Z): at 04:00 the list's first card was Cosmos 2428, `Faint, needs dark sky (+4.3)`, a weak first thing for a post to show, and at 05:00 it is Tiangong at 05:48, `Like a bright star (+0.4)`, 47 minutes out; the stored run is recomputed there (24 passes; `stored-run-neuquen.json` unchanged). **"Nothing after it is shown" covers a held instant**: the phone's live flow opens at `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` instead of twelve hours on — nothing is up at 05:00, so `[ see this pass ]` is offered and holds Tiangong's 05:48 pass — and it takes no minute steps, since that pass lasts 40 s and a step leaves it behind (`0 up`); the desk's flow steps a minute at a time along Tiangong's 07:20 pass and never takes `[ pass ▶| ]`, whose next rise is the evening's. `SHOWCASE_BY_DAY` is gone. **The review's finding is fixed here rather than filed**: `promoFlows.ts` read the stored run at import and threw when no Tiangong pass rose in the 10:20 UTC minute, and `playwright.config.ts` imports it, so a regenerated run would have failed every Playwright run at load; `BRIGHTEST_PASS` is now the literal `48274-1788690047813` and `showcase.test.ts` holds it to the run. The seeds' test gains two assertions: the first pass after `SHOWCASE_NIGHT` is Tiangong at 05:48 and brighter than `FAINT_MAG`, and the phone flow's next rise is 05:48 while the recording spec never uses `data-step="next-rise"`. **The phone's `.mp4` is cropped and scaled**: Chromium's screencast captures the page at its CSS size and ignores the device pixel ratio, so every phone video since P4 carried the page in the top-left 390 × 844 of its 1170 × 2532 frame and grey padding in the rest (D-652 and P4's Done note foresaw a capped frame, not a padded one). The conversion now crops a flow's viewport out and scales it to its device's frame with `lanczos` wherever the two differ; the desk's, equal, are converted as before. The text is softer than a still's; a frame-by-frame build from DPR-3 screenshots would be sharp and is left for a later task. The `.webm` stays the unedited record.

- **D-691 — P8: the set on the showcase night, what the night lacks, and a guard for US-36 AC8.** (P8; FR-SHOW-9, FR-SHOW-10, FR-CAP-1..5; applies D-684, D-685.) **The glare pass:** the stored Bariloche run has five passes before `SHOWCASE_UNTIL` and none with `moonGlare.glare` (the nearest is the 05:48 Tiangong pass, 8.3° from the Moon and not flagged), so `GLARE_PASS` became `SHOWN_PASS`, the night's brightest (`BRIGHTEST_PASS`, Tiangong at 07:20:47 local), and the guide, polar and window files are shot on it; `showcase.test.ts` asserts the absence, so the day a regenerated run has a glare pass the test says so. **The `Next ISS` tag:** only the ISS is `featured`, and the 72 h run has no ISS pass, so no card on the night has a tag; `captureSeeds.listSettled` waited for one and now waits for the first card, as `promo-record.spec.ts`'s `homeSettled` already did. **The chip's instant** moved from eight minutes before the pass to three (`SHOWN_PASS_START - 3 * 60_000`): eight minutes over Paris was inside the lookahead of another pass; over Bariloche it is outside `ARC_LOOKAHEAD_MS` for the only pass coming, and at three minutes the 07:04 pass has set, so the field is empty and the chip names Tiangong `139° right, up in 2:50`. **The legend** at `SHOWN + 2 min` has one drawn row, `up`: the night's passes do not overlap, so no instant holds `soon` or `gone` beside another, and nothing hidden is above the horizon in the twilight, so the FR-LIVE-6 rows are absent; the `what` line says so and the instant is unchanged. **The home's closed nights** (D-179): the night has five passes and the 72 h nineteen, so the open default would no longer make an unreviewable file; the route is kept so the set's shape and its `-view` pairing do not change. **A guard:** every capture now fails before its shot if the page's visible text holds `UTC`, a cloud badge without a forecast, the readiness or failure line about the forecast, or FR-SAT-4's warning, in either language — US-36 AC8 as a check rather than a look. **The run:** 254 passed in 1.9 min on a ten-core Mac against `npm run build`; 230 files changed against `main` (the 24 unchanged are `location`, which has no place yet, and `shortcuts`, whose overlay covers the page). A second local run differed in 16 files by 3 to 10 pixels of at most 2 levels on bar and stripe edges (`legend-360`, `live-scrubbing` at 1200, 1920 and 3840, `live-watching` at 360 and 1024): D-611's sub-pixel noise on this machine, not the instant (every clock is pinned and asserted to the second). The first run is the committed set; FR-CAP-5's reading of record is `captures.yml` twice on the branch head. **Seen at the re-shoot and left** (D-656): F-101, the saved-places row on a phone wrapping round a geocoded label.
- **D-696 — The dome flows: London at 21:18 on the 6th, played at 60×.** (P9; FR-SHOW-6 and FR-SHOW-9 as amended, V22-20.) `observers.ts` gains `LONDON_QUERY`, `LONDON` (the first `Place` of `parseGeocodeBody` over `2026-09-06-london-geocode.json`, through `observerFromPlace`, as `BARILOCHE` is built), `DOME_NIGHT = 2026-09-06T20:18:00Z` (21:18 BST) and `STORED_RUN_LONDON_FILE`; `scripts/build-stored-run.ts` writes the London run there (170 passes in 72 h; the Neuquén and Bariloche runs byte for byte unchanged). `stubNetwork`'s `'showcase'` weather reads a table of places — each forecast with the cell its `.meta.json` names, each geocode with its query — so it answers Bariloche's and London's requests and refuses every other. `promoFlows.ts` gains two `dome-playback` flows, phone and desk, `at: DOME_NIGHT`, 32 s, stills `crowded` and `overhead`; the spec stores the London run and reloads (the `homeAtBariloche` method), opens the live page, enters scrubbing, presses `live-play` at the default 60× and watches 29 s of wall time — 21:18 to about 21:48 of sky — before pausing. The stills a test shot are keyed by flow and device, since the two share a name. Computed with the worker handler over the committed elements: from 20:19 UTC eleven passes cross in 26 minutes, ten brighter than `FAINT_MAG`, up to five up at once (Tiangong at −0.8, Terra, Okean-O at 88°, five rocket bodies). The flows' sky ends at about 20:48 UTC, under `SHOWCASE_UNTIL`. `showcase.test.ts` holds the observer, the cell, the clear 20:00 UTC sample, the run and the window's counts.

### 2.38 v2.3 decisions (2026-10-19)

The phase changes one thing on screen (F-98) and otherwise renames what is there. Its decisions are how the sheet and the primitives are laid out so that the tests can read them, what the literals test matches and exempts, where the dev page lives so that it is served and never built, and why the eight tasks run one at a time. SPEC §5.11 is adopted except where a row below says otherwise.

- **D-700 — The sheet is sections the tests parse; night is a colour set the test compares.** (FR-DS-1, FR-THEME-1 as amended; V23-3.) `tokens.css` is re-cut under seven markers, `/* == grid == */`, `space`, `type`, `edges`, `layers`, `colour`, and the `[data-theme='night']` block, in that order; `scripts/contrast.ts`'s `readTokens` gains `readSections(css)`, which returns each section's tokens in order, and the guide and both style tests read the sheet through it rather than by their own regexes. Every length section is written in `:root` only, from `--row` (`1.5rem`, 24 px at the base) and `--cell` (`1ch`) as `calc()`; `tests/styles/tokens.test.ts` asserts that the night block's token set equals the colour section's and nothing else (V23-3 as a test, not a convention), that every token in `space`, `edges` and `layers` has a `calc(`, `var(` or integer value and no bare length, and that the four reserved chart tokens (FR-DS-8) meet their ratios in both themes. The type ladder keeps every size-and-line-height pair in use at `ed8748a` — six rem sizes above `--small` (2, 1.5, 1.375, 1.25, 1.125 and 1 rem) on five line heights (2.375, 1.75, 1.625, 1.125 rem and 1) — as `--text-<role>` / `--text-<role>-row` pairs named for the role of the element that uses them (`title`, `tagline`, `heading`, `lead`, `body`, …), never for the size, so a later collapse (OQ-37) is a value change and not a rename; the sheet task picks the roles from where each pair is used and records the table in its decision block. The chart's pixel sizes become `--chart-text-9`, `-11`, `-12`, `-14`, `-15`, named for the size on purpose (OQ-38). `--space-block` is `1.2rem` beside the space scale with a comment naming FR-FIRST-1/2 (V23-5).
- **D-701 — The literals test: what it matches, what it exempts, and how the allow-list only falls.** (FR-DS-2; V23-7.) `tests/styles/literals.test.ts` walks `src/**/*.css` except `tokens.css`, strips comments, and matches: a hex, `rgb(`, `hsl(`, `color-mix(` with a literal inside, or a CSS named colour other than `transparent`, `currentColor` and `inherit`; a `px`, `rem` or `em` number other than `0` **outside an `@media` or `@container` condition** (those are `breakpoint.test.ts`'s, D-702); `z-index:` followed by a digit; `outline` other than `outline-offset: var(--focus-offset-tight)`; `font-family:` whose value is not `var(--font-mono)`; and `content:` of `"[ "` or `" ]"` in a file outside `ui/components/primitives/`. For `src/ui/**/*.tsx` it matches `style={{ … }}` objects whose values are a colour or a length literal; a custom property (`'--x': …`) and a number computed at runtime are allowed, which is what the eleven inline styles at `ed8748a` set. `tests/styles/literals.allow.json` is `{ "<path>": { "count": n, "reason": "…" } }`, keyed by file so two tasks lowering two files touch two lines; the test fails when a file's matches exceed its count **and when they fall short of it**, so lowering a count is part of the change that earns it, and an entry at zero is a failure (it must be removed). The sheet task seeds the file at the day's counts and every later task lowers its own files; `R110` asserts the file is empty but for the entries the phase names (the chart modules' runtime geometry, if any remain) with their reasons.
- **D-702 — Breakpoints stay pixel literals in the modules and constants in `layout.ts`; the test is the join.** (FR-DS-3; V23-9, V23-10.) CSS cannot read a TypeScript constant, so every `@media` and `@container` condition keeps its number in the module as today, and `tests/styles/breakpoint.test.ts` holds each to an export of `lib/layout.ts`: the existing widths, the three heights `SIDEWAYS_MAX_HEIGHT_PX` (500), `SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT_PX` (700) and `WIDE_SHORT_MAX_HEIGHT_PX` (720), and `FRAME_LEGEND_MIN_CELLS` (62, `ChartFrame.module.css`'s container query, D-259). The test gains a syntax rule — every condition is `(width >= …)`, `(width <= …)`, `(height <= …)` or `(min-width: …ch)` in a container query — and a listing: it collects every condition in the tree as `(feature, comparator, value)` and compares the set to a committed list, `tests/styles/breakpoints.json`, so the rewrite to range syntax is proved to change no size by the list being identical before and after (the sheet task commits the list first, rewrites, and the test stays green). The floor this sets, Safari 16.4 / Chrome 104 / Firefox 63, is written in §11 and in `docs/DESIGN.md`'s rules; nothing in the tree targets anything older.
- **D-703 — A primitive is one `.tsx`, one `.module.css` and one manifest row; the manifest is the join between the guide, the dev page and the test.** (FR-DS-4, FR-DS-6; V23-4, V23-6.) `src/ui/components/primitives/` holds `TextButton`, `BracketLink`, `OptionToggle` and `ToggleGroup`, `Card`, `Rule` and `SectionHeading`, `Line`, `Field`, `Stack`, `Cluster` and `VisuallyHidden` — `OptionToggle` and `SectionHeading` move there from `common/` with their tests, their imports updated in the same task. `manifest.ts` exports `PRIMITIVES: readonly PrimitiveEntry[]` with `name`, `file`, `props` (name, type as a string, one sentence) and `when` (one sentence on when it is the right one); `primitives/manifest.test.ts` asserts every `.tsx` in the directory but the manifest and the tests has a row and every row a file, and that each row's `props` match the component's exported `Props` type by name (a type-level check: each entry's `props` is typed as `(keyof XProps)[]`). Primitives are leaves: an ESLint zone forbids `src/ui/components/primitives` importing `src/state`, `src/lib`, `src/i18n`, `src/data` and any other `src/ui/**` directory, so a primitive carries no copy and no behaviour of the app, only props. A feature component composes them and keeps its file and its name (`FailureLine` renders a `Line`, `PassCard` a `Card`, `SortToggle` a `ToggleGroup`, `CoordsInput` a `Field`), which is what keeps `controlRows.test.ts`, the component tests and the captures unchanged.
- **D-704 — The ring is `global.css`'s, the brackets are the two control primitives', and the clip rule is `VisuallyHidden`'s.** (FR-DS-1 edges, FR-DS-4; FR-A11Y.) `global.css` keeps the one `:focus-visible` rule, written from `--focus-ring` and `--focus-offset`; the ten modules that restate an outline lose it, and `TimeStripe` and `StripeOverview` keep `outline-offset: var(--focus-offset-tight)` alone (the one `outline` form D-701 allows). The `[ label ]` brackets exist in `TextButton.module.css` and `BracketLink.module.css` only, and the 21 modules that draw them today lose the `::before`/`::after`, the reset and the accent together — a feature module may set a grid area or a margin from the space scale on a primitive and nothing else. The visually-hidden block leaves `global.css` and `App.module.css` for `VisuallyHidden.module.css`; `global.css` keeps the base, the ring and the shape rules.
- **D-705 — `ToggleGroup` is the row; the three private toggles become it.** (FR-DS-4 item 3; V23-4.) `ToggleGroup` renders `OptionToggle`s under `role="radiogroup"` (or `group` for a multi-select row) with an accessible name, arrow-key movement between options and the pressed state in text as today (`[x]`, FR-X-5); the chart view control, the sort row (`SortToggle`), the playback toggle and the speeds (`PlaybackControls`'s two copies) are groups. `SortToggle` and `PlaybackControls` keep their files and their copy and lose their own `[x]` markup and CSS. The DOM a group renders is the DOM those rows render today — the same roles, the same text — so `controlRows.test.ts`, the live e2e and the captures do not move; where a row's accessible structure differs today, the task records which and keeps the better one, and the captures decide.
- **D-706 — The dev page is a root HTML entry `vite` serves and `vite build` never sees; its captures have their own config.** (FR-DS-6; V23-6.) `dev/primitives.html` and `dev/primitives.tsx` sit at the root beside `spike/`, served by `npm run dev` the way the spike pages are (Vite serves any HTML under the root), excluded from the build because `index.html` is the only input, and ignored by `tests/build/` and the budget by construction. The page imports `PRIMITIVES` and the components, renders every primitive in every state and tone, in both themes side by side (two `data-theme` subtrees, so one page shows both), at compact (390 px, `data-compact`) and wide. `playwright.design.config.ts` is a wrapper on `playwright.config.ts` whose `webServer` is `npx vite --port ${PORT} --strictPort` and whose `testMatch` is `tests/e2e/design-captures.spec.ts`; `npm run design:captures` runs it and writes `docs/screenshots/design/design-primitives-{390,1280}-{dark,night}.png` (four files, English — primitives carry no copy of their own); `captureSet.ts` gains a `design` group read by `tests/docs/captures.test.ts`, and `captures.yml` gains the step after the set. CSP is not a concern: the dev server does not send `_headers`.
- **D-707 — `docs/DESIGN.md` is written by `scripts/design-guide.ts` from the sheet, the manifest and one static block, and `tests/docs/design.test.ts` regenerates it in memory and compares.** (FR-DS-6, FR-DS-9; V23-6.) The script reads `tokens.css` through `readSections` and prints each section as a table — token, dark value, night value where there is one, and the contrast the tokens test computes for the pairs it checks (`contrast.ts`'s table) — then the primitives from the manifest (name, props, `when`), then the rules of SPEC §4.45 in plain words as a block the script carries (FR-DS-2's list, FR-DS-3's syntax and floor, FR-DS-4's "a prop, never an override", FR-DS-9's order of work and the handoff rule), then the four design captures as images. The test runs the generator and expects the committed file byte for byte (the `accuracy.test.ts` pattern, D-650), so the guide cannot drift from the sheet or the manifest; `docs/HOW-THIS-WAS-BUILT.md`'s reading order names it (FR-PUB-2) and `README.md` links it once.
- **D-708 — F-98 is one token swap, one deleted opacity and one deleted exception; the set is re-shot on `captures.yml` and the diff is the release note.** (FR-DS-5, FR-DS-7; V23-5.) `SkyDome.module.css`'s `.degree` reads `color: var(--chart-compass)` and loses `opacity: 0.8`; `tests/e2e/axe.spec.ts` loses the `color-contrast` exclusion for those nodes, and the axe run is what proves the move. The re-shoot is the workflow's run on the branch (FR-CAP-5's two runs, F-99's reading), not the Mac's; the list of files that differ from `ed8748a`'s set is the PR's and `docs/RELEASE.md` §14's, and every file not on it is byte-identical. The budget table from `npm run bundle:budget` on the branch is in the same PR: main and the stylesheet within 1.5 KB gzipped of `ed8748a`'s measure, no row raised (FR-DS-7).
- **D-709 — Eight `R` tasks, one at a time, each across every lane.** (SPEC §9 Phase 2k; D-655's rule.) The sheet task rewrites every stylesheet's media queries and seeds the allow-list; each primitive task deletes CSS in `ui`, `live`, `chart` and `window` modules and lowers the allow-list; the guide task reads the manifest the primitives wrote; the re-shoot needs every module settled. No two can share a wave without sharing files, so each runs alone as `ui` with every lane's directories in scope, as `P5` did (D-655), in eight waves of one. The cost is calendar time, about a day of sessions; the alternative — cutting each primitive by lane into three tasks — would triple the briefs, the reviews and the allow-list hunks for no parallelism, since every task would still wait on the sheet and on the primitive's first task. Model and review as v2.2 (D-659): `fable`, reviewed on `opus`, `Turns: 500`, `Fallback: off`.

### 2.39 R103 and R104 decisions (2026-10-19)

- **D-710 — The type ladder, named by role.** (FR-DS-1, D-700; R103.) Every size-and-line-height pair in use at `ed8748a`, one `--text-<role>` / `--text-<role>-row` pair each, named for the element that sets it and never for the size; `--small` / `--small-row` kept as they are. The table, from the modules as they stood (no value changes, FR-DS-5):

  | Pair | Size | Row | Where it is set |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `--text-title` | 2rem (32) | 2.375rem (38) | `NextEventBlock` `.time` — the next event's time on the home |
  | `--text-countdown` | 1.5rem (24) | `calc(2 * var(--row))` (48) | `Countdown` `.headline` — the pass detail's live countdown |
  | `--text-question` | 1.375rem (22) | 1.75rem (28) | `App` `.coldHeading`, `Steps` `.heading` — the compact first-run question (FR-FIRST-1) |
  | `--text-pane` | 1.25rem (20) | 1.625rem (26) | the wide `.coldHeading`, `App` `.ghostHeading`, `NextEventBlock` `.cardTime` — the wide board's question and pane headings, the next-event card's time |
  | `--text-heading` | 1.25rem (20) | `var(--row)` (24) | `PassDetail` `.heading`, `GuidePanel` `.heading` (which inherit the row), `TimeReadout` `.readout`, `Live` `.headline [data-testid='next-event-time']` |
  | `--text-lead` | 1.125rem (18) | `calc(1.25 * var(--row))` (30) | `GuideText` `.guide` — the guide's prose |
  | `--text-body` | 1rem (16) | `var(--row)` (24) | `global.css` `h1`–`h3`, `PassCard` `.name`, `TimeStripe` `.hour`/`.date`, `TimeReadout` `.offset` |
  | `--text-stripe` | `var(--small)` (14) | 1.125rem (18) | `TonightStripe` `.stripe`, `App` `.ghostStripe` |
  | `--chart-text-9` … `-15` | 9, 11, 12, 14, 15 px | — | the charts' SVG and dome text, in px on purpose (OQ-38): the degree labels, the dome's labels and the polar key, the compass and the dome key, the window's key, the window's major compass points |

  Two things the table decided. The 1.25 rem size is two pairs and not one, because it sits on two rows — the board's 26 px (`--text-pane`) and the body's 24 px (`--text-heading`) — and a pair is the unit, so collapsing them later (OQ-37) is a value change on one row. The unitless `line-height: 1` the dome, the sky screen and the chart text use is a ratio and not a length — the literals test does not match it and it is not a token — so the chart's text tokens are sizes alone. The modules still write the values: R103 touches a module for the query rewrite only, and R104–R107 swap each literal for its name as they rebuild the component it is in (the allow-list's counts fall with them, D-701).

- **D-711 — The hairline is the grid's one bare pixel; every other length in the sheet is a share of the row.** (FR-DS-1, D-700; R103.) FR-DS-1 writes `--border` as `1px solid var(--rule)` and asks that every length be written from `--row` or `--cell`; one device pixel is not a share of a 24 px row, and `calc(var(--row) / 24)` would be 1.25 px for a reader whose base font is 20 px — a border that is sometimes two device pixels, for no reason the grid has. So the grid section carries `--hairline: 1px` beside `--cell`, `--row` and `--tap` (the one bare length outside the type ladder, as `breakpoint.test.ts` has always exempted `1px` as a hairline), and the edges section names it: `--border: var(--hairline) solid var(--rule)`, `--border-control: var(--hairline) solid var(--edge)`, `--radius-1: var(--hairline)`, `--focus-offset-tight: var(--hairline)`. The 2 px values are `calc(var(--row) / 12)` — `--radius-2`, `--focus-ring`, `--focus-offset` — which `SkyScreen.module.css` already wrote that way; `--gutter` stays `28px`, a px on purpose like the chart text tokens: `GUTTER_PX` in `window/gutter.ts` places the chip and the notes from the same number in script, so a value that scaled with the base font would leave the drawing and its gutter apart at any base but 16 px (the review of #172 caught the first draft writing it as `calc(7 * var(--row) / 6)`); `tests/styles/gutter.test.ts` holds the two equal and, since R103, can also read a `calc(K * var(--row) / M)`. `tests/styles/tokens.test.ts` holds `space`, `edges` and `layers` to a `calc()`, a `var()`, an integer, a percentage or `0`, with `--space-block` the one named exception (1.2 rem, V23-5). Every value is the same number of pixels it was at the base size.

- **D-712 — The four star tokens are in `CHART_MARK_TOKENS` and out of the dome's palette.** (FR-DS-8; R103.) `scripts/contrast.ts` lists `--chart-star`, `--chart-star-dim`, `--chart-figure` and `--chart-planet` among the marks, so the tokens test measures them with the rest (≥ 3 : 1 in both themes, documented beside each value, the night value a red hue), and holds them to FR-DS-8's own bars — 10, 4.5, 3 and 7 : 1 — with the planet apart from the star by more than one ratio point in both themes and by more than 90° of hue in dark. `CHART_RESERVED_TOKENS` names the four, and `dome/palette.test.tsx` expects the dome's palette to name every mark but those: nothing draws with them in this phase, as nothing drew with the R16 tokens before R21. Dark values: star `#e3e8ee` (15.60 : 1), dim star `#8a94a1` (6.25), figure `#5a7088` (3.76), planet `#f2c27a` (11.69, gold against the stars' white); night: `#ffc0b0` (13.12), `#cc5848` (4.95), `#9b4238` (3.16), `#ff9a70` (9.89).

- **D-713 — The header's four folds join `layout.ts`; the script's queries take the range syntax too; `<` stays `<`.** (FR-DS-3, D-702; R103.) D-702 holds *every* condition to an export of `lib/layout.ts`, and the header's four `width <` folds (D-546: 973 and 848 px in English, 1089 and 1050 in Spanish) had none — `controlRows.test.ts` recomputes them from the catalog. They are now `HEADER_FOLD_PX`, a literal record like `FOOTER_ONE_LINE_MIN_PX`, held from both sides: `controlRows.test.ts` to the catalog, `breakpoint.test.ts` to the stylesheet. D-702's syntax rule names `(width <= …)`; the folds and D-681's footer rule are written `(width < …)`, the exact complement of a `(width >= …)` threshold, and rewriting them to `<=` would move each by a pixel, so the rule as tested is `width >=`, `width <`, `height <=`, or an orientation, and `(min-width: …ch)` in the one container query — which stays in the form D-702 names, the one `SkyChart.contract.test.tsx` reads the beside-the-drawing block by. `WIDE_QUERY`, `HOME_THREE_PANE_QUERY` and `LANDSCAPE_PHONE_QUERY` — what `useLayoutMode`, `App` and `usePageShape` ask `matchMedia` — are range syntax as well, so the script and the stylesheet ask the browser one question in one form (the e2e helpers evaluate `WIDE_QUERY` in Chromium; `tests/support/matchMedia.ts` reads both forms, since older tests still write `min-width`). `LANDSCAPE_PHONE_MAX_HEIGHT_PX` is renamed `SIDEWAYS_MAX_HEIGHT_PX`, the name the spec gives the number; nothing but its own test read it. The listing in `tests/styles/breakpoints.json` is per file in source order, each query as `@media width >= 964px and height <= 720px`, and was committed (`f15b55b`) before the rewrite; the rewrite left it byte-identical.

- **D-714 — `OptionToggle` is one option and `ToggleGroup` is the row; every row keeps `role="group"` and `aria-pressed`, and the radiogroup form waits.** (FR-DS-4 item 3, D-705; R104.) D-705 names `OptionToggle` as what a `ToggleGroup` renders, so the component R13 wrote — a whole `[x] a [ ] b` group — is re-cut: `OptionToggle` is one `[x] option`, a pressed-state button whose `label`, `pressed`, `onPress`, `value` (as `data-option`, R66) and `alone` (the live page's hidden-objects toggle, with no trailing cell) are its whole surface; `ToggleGroup` is the row — `name`, `prefix`, `options`, `value`, `onChange`, and three *marks*: `check` (`[x] option`, an `OptionToggle` each), `bracket` (the sort row's `Sort: [ Soonest ] Best`, FR-FIRST-10) and `tight` (the compact speeds' `1× [60×] 600×`, D-245), the last two `TextButton`s with `pressed`, since the brackets are drawn there and nowhere else (D-704); `gap="none"` is the wide speeds (D-172). Every row the app has today renders `role="group"` with `aria-pressed` buttons, so that is the group's default and the DOM of every row is unchanged — `controlRows.test.ts`, `PlaybackControls.test.tsx`, the live e2e and the captures count on it — and the `role="radiogroup"` form (`aria-checked`, one tab stop, the arrows choose) is built and tested but no row is moved onto it: D-705 says the task keeps the better structure where the two differ, and today's rows do not differ from one another, so there is nothing to pick between; a later task may move the single-choice rows to it as one accessibility change with its own captures. The arrow keys move between the options in both forms and wrap.

- **D-715 — `TextButton`'s forms are the forms the 21 modules drew, one prop each; the reset leaves the block padding alone; what a feature module still says about a control after R104, and why.** (FR-DS-4 item 1, FR-DS-5, D-704; R104.) The spec's five props (`label`, `onClick`, `disabled`, `tone`, `pressed`) draw one of the forms in the tree; the others are the props, each named for the module that needed it so no pixel moves (FR-DS-5): `inline` (the `inline-control` tap box hung off a line of prose — `FailureLine`'s details, the banners, the notices, `WherePlace`, the home's more controls, `NextEventBlock`'s `[ see this pass ]`, the settings way back, Live's compact Back), `tight` (with `pressed`, D-245), `bare` (the words without the brackets, `ShareButton`'s `plain`, D-411), `padded` (a cell inside at each side and a `--tap` floor on the width, `GuidePanel`'s `[ × ]` and `[ to list ]`), `box="edge"` (the sheet's bordered button, `PassDetail`'s way back and the share action), `box="accent"` with `fill` and `tall` (the home's `[ continue ]` and the when step's 56 px `[ See what crosses ]`), `note` with `look` (the primary `[ Use my location ]`, its line under the label as `aria-describedby`, boxed on a phone and plain in the wide pane, FR-FIRST-2), `wrap` (a saved place's name) and `as="summary"` (the error page's disclosure, FR-FAIL-5). Two things the first cut got wrong and the conversion fixed: the reset is `padding-inline: 0` and never `padding: 0`, because a module class outranks `global.css`'s `.inline-control` at equal specificity and a `padding: 0` there took the 48 px box off every inline control; and the bracket rules are written one selector per rule, never a list, because `tests/styles/cells.ts` reads `.class[state]::before` off the file and skips a selector list. What a feature module still says about a control is placement — `Favourites` `.remove` (`margin-inline-start: auto`), `UseMyLocation` `.device` (`width: max-content; max-width: 100%` in the field's grid, which is what the old `.button` set and the only reason the settings row is one line), `PassDetail` `.close` (`justify-self`), `Steps` `.next` (`margin-top: auto`), `Live` `.back` (`flex: 0 0 auto` on compact) — and three rules that are not brackets and stay where they are for the task that takes D-704's outlines and resets out of the feature modules: F-100's `.page[data-compact] .back:focus-visible` (the 0 px offset and the fold's collapse), and `Live.module.css`'s `[data-fold] button` and compact `.actions button` rules, which give every button on the folded rail the tap box and strip the share's border — they outrank the primitive's `.edge` and still do, so the live page is unchanged, but each is a restyle a prop should replace. `NextEventBlock`'s `[ see this pass ]` gains `inline-control`'s focus rule (the ring round the text line, R75), which it had written the padding of but not the focus of; nothing else about any control's focus changes. **One visible change, named here against FR-DS-5:** the primitive's base is `white-space: nowrap` — a `[ label ]` takes the rest of a line or none of it (D-246's rule, written for one control and now every control's) — and eleven of the 21 modules did not say so. The one place that shows is the saved-places row on a phone (`v1-favourites-360/390-*`, and `v1-settings-360/390-*`, which draw the same rows): the remove control `[ × ]` beside a long place name used to break *inside itself*, `[ ×` on one line and `]` on the next, and now stays whole, which moves `(in use)` and the `]` by a cell or two in those files. The task keeps the whole bracket rather than the split one and names the files; R110's re-shoot lists them beside F-98's, or the owner's gate asks for `wrap` on that control and the split comes back.

- **D-716 — What else the conversion took out, and the three edits to the test the task was told not to change.** (D-703, D-704, D-705; R104.) `SortToggle.module.css`, `UpdateBanner.module.css` and `FaintToggle.module.css` are gone, with nothing left in them once the control was the primitive's; their allow-list entries with them. `Settings.module.css`'s `.controlRow button` override — which redrew the device button as a text control on the settings row — and `UseMyLocation.module.css`'s bordered two-cell `.button` form go together: the bordered form was reachable only through that row, which restyled it, so the primitive renders the text control there and the override has nothing to do. The allow-list falls from 244 matches in 51 files to 180 in 39; every lowered entry's reason names R104 and what it took. `tests/styles/controlRows.test.ts` is "unchanged" in every row, budget and number; it changed in three places D-703 sanctions ("their imports updated in the same task"): the chart view control is built from `ToggleGroup` rather than the old group-shaped `OptionToggle`; its stylesheet list reads the brackets off the three primitive modules instead of `common/OptionToggle.module.css`, `SortToggle.module.css` and `FaintToggle.module.css`; and the header-fold arithmetic reads `.option`'s padding from `primitives/OptionToggle.module.css` and `.group`'s gap from `primitives/ToggleGroup.module.css`. The header counts 34 cells as before and every fold literal recomputes to the same number. Three components borrowed a converted module's class without being in the list of 21 — `ClearSavedLocation` (`LocationInput`'s `.clear`), `InstallHint`'s "Not now" (`InstallAction`'s `.action`) and the home's `[ continue ]` (`Steps`' `.continue`, from `Home.tsx`) — and the first re-shoot found them as a bordered box where a text control had been: a module's class list is not its consumer list, and the check that found the other two is every `styles.X` in `src/ui` resolving to a class in its module (which also turned up three dangling references older than this task, `CompassGutter` `.marker`, `SkyWindow` `.grid` and `CoordsInput` `.altField`, left for their own lanes).

- **D-718 — `Line` is the five lines' forms as props: the tone paints the marker and the edge, the sentence has an ink of its own, and the dot is text.** (FR-DS-4 item 6, FR-DS-5, FR-X-5; D-703; R105.) The spec's three props (`tone`, `children`, `actions`) draw none of the five lines by themselves, because the five do not share one look — the readiness line is a dim sentence, the banner a framed sentence with a spelled-out prefix, the failure line a sentence over a 48 px control row, the elements line a dim sentence that turns `--warn` with `[ details ]` after a dot, the visit notice a sentence and two inline controls on one line on a desk and on two rows on a phone — so each look is a prop named for it, as D-715 did for `TextButton`, and no pixel moves. `tone` (`status` dim, `ok`, `notice` `--warn`, `failure` `--danger`) paints the **marker** and, in the `box` form, the frame's left edge; a note's edge is the accent while its marker stays dim, which is R11's info banner and the one place the two inks part. The **sentence** has its own `ink` — the page's `--fg` by default (a banner's text, a failure's sentence: neither was ever coloured, and colouring the failure line red would have been the phase's third visible change), `dim` (the readiness line, a link note), or `tone` (the elements line, whose words say the age the ink underlines; FR-X-5's "the marker is the second channel" holds because every toned line either carries a marker or says it in words). `size` is `body` or `small`; `box` is the banner's frame with its `pre-wrap`; `rows` is `text` (the visit notice on a phone: the controls' row straight under the sentence, a cell between them) or `controls` (the failure line: a quarter row under, the controls centred, two cells apart — the two rows differ in both gaps, so one boolean could not be both); `dot` is ` · `. The dot is a `<span aria-hidden>` whose two spaces are **text**, not padding and not `white-space: pre`: `ElementsLine.test.tsx` reads `Elements 9 d 4 h old · details` off the line, a space is the same cell as `1ch` of padding at the same size, and the spaces break as text does — the first re-shoot caught `pre` taking the wrap after the dot away from the Spanish elements line at 360 px, which then broke before `h` instead. Without a dot the actions follow the sentence after a text space (the link note's `×`), which the `rows` grids drop. The five keep their test ids on elements the host owns — `failure-sentence` and `visit-sentence` are spans the host passes as the sentence — and the one id the host cannot place, `visit-actions`, went: `controlRows.test.ts` finds the actions row as the parent of `visit-back`. `LinkNote`, in `VisitNotice.tsx` though not in the spec's five, is the same line and was converted with its file. `Banner.module.css` is gone; the notices strip keeps its `--small` and its dim ink on the container because `--cell` is read at the container's size and its padding is written in cells.

- **D-719 — `Card` gains `section` and `frame`, and the card's ring is the one `global.css` rule's second selector.** (FR-DS-4 item 4, D-704; R105.) The spec's `as` is `article | button | a`; `NextEventBlock`'s card form is a `<section aria-label>` whose role the tests and the outline read, so `section` is the fourth element rather than a role change. `selected` is the open pass (the accent frame on the raised ground, `data-selected` for the stylesheet and `aria-current` for a reader); `frame="accent"` is the phone's first card, ruled in the accent without being selected, which `selected` alone could not say. The button and link forms take the sheet's control chrome off (`.control`: no `--tap` floor, no ground, no underline, the card's own padding) and wear `global.css`'s `:focus-visible` ring as any control does; no caller uses them yet. The ring an *article* card wore when its stretched `OpenGuide` had focus (`.card:has(> button:focus-visible)`, R84) could not stay in the card's module — D-701 counts every `outline` outside `global.css`, and a new primitive may not open a new allow-list entry — and dropping it would have moved the ring one pixel in (the button's box is the padding box), so `global.css`'s one rule gained the selector `:where([data-card]:has(> button:focus-visible))` — under `:where()`, a forgiving list, so a browser without `:has()` drops that selector alone and not the ring on every control — still one rule, one declaration, the same count, and `identity.spec.ts`'s walk (a card's control hands its ring to the card) unchanged. `OpenGuide.module.css`'s `outline: none` on the button itself stays for R107, whose task the outline restatements are. `NextEventBlock`'s card lost its `display: grid; gap: 0`: with `<p>` children at `margin: 0` a grid and a block lay out the same, and the primitive is a block.

- **D-720 — `Rule` is a presentational `<hr>`; six bare rules became one, one stayed a border written from the sheet, and the space beside a rule is the host's margin.** (FR-DS-4 item 5, FR-DS-5; R105.) `Rule` renders `<hr role="presentation">` drawn as the border it replaces — `border-top: var(--border)` on a box of no height — so the pixel row is the one the module's `border-top` drew; `presentation` because the borders were invisible to assistive technology and nothing they divide wants a separator announced. The `padding-top` that stood between a module's rule and its content is the rule's `margin-bottom` from the space scale, which is placement (D-704). Converted, each with its host saying where: `NextEventBlock`'s block (the `Rule` is the block's first child; `ruled` is a new prop, and `Live.tsx` passes `ruled={!compact}` where `Live.module.css` used to override the block's `border-top: 0; padding-top: 0` on the compact headline — a host restyle replaced by a prop, FR-DS-4's rule); the footer's one-row forms and the wide header's (`grid-column: 1 / -1`, a row of space above), both with `margin-inline: calc(-2 * var(--cell))`, because the border they replace was the padded landmark's and ran through the frame's two cells of side padding (global.css `header, main, footer`) while a child stops at the content box — the first re-shoot measured the 38 px; and the two-line-footer widths, which halved the footer's top padding from `App.module.css` (R102, D-681), now set `--footer-rule-gap: var(--space-2)` on the footer and `Footer.module.css` reads it for the rule's margin, since a host may name the space under a rule and may not pad over it — the second re-shoot found the row at 1024 px; the what step's foot, whose flex row became a two-column grid (`minmax(0, 1fr) auto`) so the rule could take a row across the text and `[ edit ]` — the same widths and the same top alignment as `space-between` gave; the boxed location group's foot (the plain look never had one, so the `Rule` is conditional on `look`); and the folded live rail (`fold.includes('actions')`, `flex: 0 0 100%`, the rail's row gap under it). **Not converted:** `StatusStrip`'s, which is a `<dl>` — its content model allows nothing but its groups, and `Live.module.css` reads the strip by its element in the fold (`.side dl { display: contents }`) — so its border is written `var(--border)` from the sheet, and its allow-list entry falls the same. The table rules of `PassNumbers` and `ShortcutsOverlay` and `PlacePicker`'s option separators are a table's and a listbox's row rules, not bare dividers, and are left as the task's out-of-scope line says. The `Live.module.css` headline override's removal and `ruled` are the one behaviour this task adds to a feature component; it draws the same.

- **D-722 — `Field` renders the input; its forms are the three inputs' forms as props, the altitude is a field in the coordinates field's trailing slot, and a message under a field is a `Line`.** (FR-DS-4 item 7, FR-DS-5, FR-FIRST-2; D-703, D-704; R106.) The spec's "a label, an input, a trailing action and a hint row" is read with the input as the primitive's own: `Field` takes the input's attributes — `value`, `placeholder`, `role`, `aria-*`, the handlers, a `ref` — and renders the `<input>` itself, so its width (`cells`, a custom property `--field-cells` the module multiplies by `--cell`; left out, the column's width) and its label's `htmlFor` are one `id` and never drift; the alternative, a slot the host fills with its own `<input>`, would have left the width and the association in two files. The forms: `size` is the label's type and the gap under it — the body half a row over the input (the settings panel), or `--small` in the dim ink 8 px over it, written `calc(var(--row) / 3)` because the board's 8 px is not on the space scale and FR-DS-5 keeps it; `labelHidden` is the altitude's label, read and not drawn; `unit` is the `0 m` box; `box` is the phone's ruled alternative (`--space-2` by a cell inside, `--border`), and the third-of-a-row padding it takes on a screen shorter than 700 px (R87, D-574) is **the primitive's own media rule**, not a `--box-pad` the group set from outside, since a host may not pad a primitive by a side channel any more than by a class — `breakpoints.json` and `breakpoint.test.ts`'s short-height file list gain `Field.module.css`, the one listing change, and `layout.ts`'s comment names it. `children` are the rows under the input: a validation message, a status, a pick list, the picker's confirmation; the two coloured ones are `Line`s (`tone="failure" ink="tone"` for a message in the danger ink, `ink="dim"` for the confirmation), which puts the colour in a primitive and leaves `CoordsInput.module.css` nothing but the panel's row and `PlacePicker.module.css` the list, the status's `margin: 0` and the panel's margin. **The unit box is the input.** The old `.altBox` was a bordered span round a borderless input with its own `outline` on `:has(input:focus-visible)` and an `outline: none` inside — two rules D-701 counts, and a new primitive opens no allow-list entry (D-719). The box is now a positioned `span` with no border round the sheet's own bordered input, the unit absolutely placed a hairline and the value's cells in from its edge (`--value-cells`, computed by `Field` from `value` and `placeholder`): the border, the ground, the `--tap` height and the ring are `global.css`'s, at the same pixels, and nothing in the module says `outline`. **The pair is one field with the other in its trailing slot.** The home group's coordinates and altitude are one `Field` (the coordinates) with the altitude `Field` as its `trailing`: a field in the slot joins the host's grid (`display: contents` on the wrapper and on it), its control in the second column of the input's row, its hidden label placed from the host (which is why `.withTrailing` is positioned), and its rows across both columns after the host's own — the exact grid `.home` drew with `display: contents` on its two wrappers. The rows come **before** the slot in the document, so the coordinates' message is read right after its input and the document order is the old one: label, input, message, hidden label, altitude box, altitude message. The second column is `max-content` — the altitude's ten cells on a phone — or `--field-trailing`, the one hook a host may set, which `CoordsInput`'s `.plain` sets to `calc(10 * var(--row) / 3)` for the wide pane's 80 px (FR-FIRST-2): the one width in the tree that is not a cell count, kept at its pixel because FR-DS-5 names no move here; folding it to 8 cells (77 px) or 9 (86 px) is a visible change for OQ-37 to call. The `.home` grid's `align-items: center` is gone — the input and the box are both `--tap` tall, so it centred nothing. The hidden label is still the `sr-only` global class; R107 moves the clip rule to `VisuallyHidden` and `Field` with it.

- **D-725 — `Stack`, `Cluster` and `VisuallyHidden`: what each sets, the hidden headings as a `SectionHeading` form, and the ring's offset as a token a control may set.** (FR-DS-4 item 8, FR-DS-1 edges, FR-DS-5; D-703, D-704; R107.) `Stack` is one grid column — `display: grid` and not a flex column, because that is what both modules it replaces drew and the two differ in nothing a stack shows — with `gap` a required step of the space scale (`1`..`5`, a class each) and `[hidden] { display: none }` so a panel closed by the attribute stays closed; every attribute passes through to the `div`. `ElementsLine`'s block and its panel and `FailureLine`'s line are stacks, and `ElementsLine.module.css`, left with nothing, is deleted (`controlRows.test.ts`'s stylesheet list loses the line, as R104 and R105 edited it). `Cluster` is a wrapping flex row on one baseline, `gap` a cell count (`1`, `2` — the default, FR-DS-1's `calc(2 * var(--cell))` — or `3`), `align="center"` for a row that mixes boxes and text, `as="p"` where the row is a sentence with its control, and a `:where()` margin reset so a host's margin wins; `ShareButton`'s row is one. Two controls wore the ring at another offset and FR-DS-5 and the task's goal keep them so: the live page's compact Back sits flush (`0`, F-100, in every compact live capture) and the sky screen's `×` at the screen's corner wears it inside its box (`−2 px`, where an outside ring is cut by the edge). Both modules now set `--focus-offset` on the control — `0`, and `calc(-1 * var(--focus-ring))` — and the one rule reads it: the offset token is what FR-DS-1 made it for, the ring is still drawn once, and D-701's test counts neither (a custom property is not an `outline`). `OpenGuide`'s `outline: none` on the stretched card button moves into `global.css` beside the card rule, under the same `:where(:has())` guard (a browser without `:has()` keeps the button's own ring, as before): the ring and its one exception are in one place, and `global.css`'s outline count goes 3 → 4 while its total falls. `Steps`' `.heading:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none }` is deleted outright — no browser at or above the floor FR-DS-3 sets draws a ring on `:focus` alone.
