- **D-728 — The dev page is the manifest walked, two theme subtrees, one capture per subtree; its config is the one second Playwright config the tree tracks.** (FR-DS-6; D-706; R108.) `dev/primitives.tsx` walks `PRIMITIVES` in manifest order and draws, under each row's name and `when` sentence, a specimen set keyed by the row's name — every prop of the row in every value, each case captioned with the props it was given — so a row without a set reads "no specimen" on the page and fails `tests/e2e/design-captures.spec.ts`, which also holds each theme column to one `[data-primitive]` per manifest row. The two columns are `<section data-theme>` subtrees under a root that carries `data-theme="dark"` (so `html[data-theme]`'s ground rule applies); `tokens.css`'s night block matches any element, so the night column restates the colours and the dark column inherits the root's, and no second stylesheet exists. The page's own `dev/primitives.css` lays the columns out as `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 60 cells), 1fr))` — two at 1280 px, one at 390 — with no breakpoint, so `breakpoint.test.ts` has nothing to list and the literals test (`src/**` only) nothing to read; the root carries `data-compact` from `WIDE_QUERY` so a capture states its mode. A design capture is one theme's subtree shot alone (`locator.screenshot`), not the viewport: a token's change in one theme is then a diff in that theme's file and the other stays byte-identical, and at 390 the stacked page would otherwise have put the night column off the frame. The page is static — no clock, no network, no animation — and two runs on the Mac agreed to the byte. `playwright.design.config.ts` spreads the committed config and overrides `testMatch`, the one `chromium` project, `baseURL` and `webServer` (`npx vite --port 5173 --strictPort`, `DESIGN_PORT` to move it, the F-20 `reuseExistingServer` expression restated): the dev server's port and not `E2E_PORT`, because a `vite preview` left on 4173 by an e2e run would be adopted locally and has no dev page to serve. `.gitignore`'s `/playwright.*.config.*` would have ignored the file, so it gains `!/playwright.design.config.ts` under the two patterns, and `hygiene.test.ts` now expects exactly the two configs and the negation line (F-16/F-20's rule kept: nothing else gets past the patterns). `tsconfig.app.json` includes `dev/` so the page is typechecked with the app; `knip.json` names `dev/primitives.tsx` as an entry (the config knip finds by itself).

- **D-729 — The guide is five length tables, one colour table with the computed contrast, the manifest and a rules block; the node project gains JSX to type-check the manifest.** (FR-DS-6, FR-DS-9; D-707; R108.) `scripts/design-guide.ts` exports `renderGuide(css)`: the five `:root` sections as `Token | Value | Note` tables, the note being the trailing comment on the token's line (`readNotes`, the first occurrence per name, so the dark line and never the night block's ratio); the colour section as `Token | Dark | Night | Contrast, dark | Contrast, night | Note`, the contrast cell computed from the values with `contrast.ts`'s own `contrastRatio` against the pairs the tokens test checks — a text token on both grounds (and `--bg` on `--accent`), the edge on both, the rule on `--bg`, every chart mark and surface on `--bg`, the four reserved marks named as FR-DS-8's — so the figures agree with the sheet's header by construction and the night ratio is never copied; then one block per manifest row (file, `when`, a `Prop | Type | What it does` table, pipes escaped); then the rules of SPEC §4.45 in plain words, held in the script as the one input that changes with the spec and not with the files; then the four design captures as images. Nothing reads the clock or the tree, which is what makes `tests/docs/design.test.ts`'s byte-for-byte compare fair; the test also holds the guide to naming every token of every section with its value, every night value, every primitive with its file and every prop with its type, the floor sentence and the four images, so a renderer that printed nothing could not pass against a committed nothing. `accuracy.test.ts`'s document list gains `docs/DESIGN.md` (every path and script it names exists — D-650's rule, one document wider). The manifest's `import type` lines resolve to `.tsx` files, and `tsc` refuses a `.tsx` in a project without `jsx` whatever the import's kind, so `tsconfig.node.json` — the project that compiles `scripts/`, `tests/docs` and `tests/e2e` — gains `"jsx": "react-jsx"`, the DOM libs and `vite/client`'s types (for the components' `.module.css` imports); the Playwright specs already pulled the DOM lib in through `@playwright/test`, so nothing in the project changed meaning.

- **D-730 — The design group is four files in a directory of their own, English only, shot by `captures.yml` after the set and uploaded as a second artefact.** (FR-DS-6, FR-CAP-1; D-706; R108.) `captureSet.ts` exports `DESIGN_PAGE`, `DESIGN_CAPTURE_DIR` (`docs/screenshots/design`), `DESIGN_FILE` (`design-primitives-<width>-<theme>.png`) and `designCaptureSet()` — 390 and 1280 by dark and night — and `captures.test.ts` holds the directory to those four the way it holds `docs/screenshots/` to the `v1-` set: every file present and non-empty, nothing the group does not name. No `-es` twin: the primitives carry no copy (D-703), so the Spanish file would be the same picture. `captures.yml` clears and shoots the four after the set and before the completeness check, so the check covers them, and uploads them as `design-captures` beside `v1-captures` (a second step rather than a second `path` line, which `ci.test.ts`'s literal match on the first would not accept); the CI job's `npm ci`, Chromium and checkout are what the dev server needs, and the build step before it is unused by this run but harmless.

The gate's items — the dev page in both themes and the guide read — are the owner's; the captures and `docs/DESIGN.md` in the PR are the material. Follow-up: the page shows no focused control, since the ring is `global.css`'s `:focus-visible` and cannot be forced from markup; a `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` before the shot would focus the dark column's first control only, so it was left for R110's gate to decide.

- **D-732 — R109's result: F-98's labels moved, the set differs from `ed8748a`'s in 148 files, the two local runs agree to F-99's noise, and the phase's main chunk is 1.9 KB over the base.** (FR-DS-5, FR-DS-7; D-708, D-727; R109.) `SkyDome.module.css`'s `.degree` reads `color: var(--chart-compass)` and has no opacity; `axe.spec.ts`'s `AXE_DISABLED_RULES` is empty and the 24 axe tests pass with `color-contrast` running on every node — the labels measure 13.8 : 1 dark and 9.3 : 1 night, the token's own ratios. ### 2.39 v2.4 decisions, first cut (2026-10-23)

V24-8 puts a spike before anything else in the phase: the catalogue's size, the draw rate with 900 text nodes, the render path and the glyph sizes are numbers the spec cannot know, and FR-STAR-9 makes the render path a plan decision taken before the page task is cut. This cut plans the spike and nothing after it. The second cut (v0.12) reads `docs/stars/FINDINGS.md` and plans the catalogue, the scene and camera, the page, the screen's inventory and the release preparation, with their decisions from D-748.

- **D-740 — The spike is one page under `spike/stars/`, served by the window spike's server, importing the app and never editing it.** (FR-STAR-12; V24-8, V11-9.) `spike/stars/index.html` and `main.tsx` render one window-shaped field. Every knob is a URL parameter read by `spike/stars/params.ts`: `render=react|ref` (positions through React state, as `SkyWindow` draws today, or written to the nodes' `x`/`y` by ref outside render); `mark=glyph|disc`; `layers=` any of `stars,figures,planets,names`; `mag` (the limit, default 4.5); `big` and `small` (the ladder's two sizes in px, default 15 and 12, the sheet's `--chart-text-15` and `--chart-text-12`); `collide` (the collision distance as a fraction of the small cell, default 0.5); `source=sensor|hand`; `facing`, `tilt` and `fov` (default `WINDOW_FOV`); `at` (an ISO instant, default now); `lat` and `lon` (default the three R1 sites by name, `site=neuquen|paris|singapore`). The projection, the rotation and the upright camera are imported from `src/ui/components/guide/skychart/window/projection.ts`, the sensor path and the rate meter from `spike/window/sensors.ts`, the positions from `astronomy-engine`'s `Rotation_EQJ_HOR`, as FR-STAR-2 will use them. The spike changes no file under `src/`. It is served at `/spike/stars/` by the HTTPS dev server `npm run spike:window` already starts, since Vite serves every HTML file under the root; `package.json` gains `spike:stars` as the same command, for the name, and `spike:stars:measure` for the scripts below.
- **D-741 — What the spike measures, and the five answers.** (FR-STAR-1, FR-STAR-2, FR-STAR-6, FR-STAR-9, FR-STAR-12; OQ-39.) Four scripts under `spike/stars/`, run by `npm run spike:stars:measure`, and the owner on a phone. **(1) The catalogue:** `catalog.ts` builds the spike's catalogue from `data-src/stars/` (D-743) — every star at V ≤ the limit, every fainter figure endpoint, the figures snapped to the nearest star — and prints its star count, its figure count, the worst snap distance, and its size raw and gzipped as JSON objects and as columns (one array per field). It writes into `.sdd-cache/spike-stars/`, which the tree ignores. **(2) The rate:** the page shows the meter's updates per second. The owner reads it on the phone under the sensor and under a drag, for the four combinations of `render` and `mark` with every layer on. `perf.ts` measures the same four by D-62's method (a 5 s drag in Playwright's Chromium, the Pixel 5 profile, 4× CPU throttling), so the number can be reproduced without the phone. **(3) The precession path:** `precession.ts` holds the rotation against the three fixtures and prints the worst separation per site. **(4) The ladder and the collision distance:** `capture.ts` shoots Crux over Neuquén and Orion over Paris at 390 × 844 and 1280 × 800, for the default ladder and two alternatives on each side, into `docs/stars/captures/`. `docs/stars/FINDINGS.md` answers, each with a number or a capture behind it: **OQ-39's figure source** (d3-celestial unless the snap fails); **`STARS_BUDGET_KB`** and the catalogue's encoding; **the render path** FR-STAR-9 names, with V24-9 held or reopened by the 30-updates/s rule; **the precession path's worst error** against `STAR_TOLERANCE_DEG`; and **the two sizes and the collision distance** the owner picks, judged on whether Crux keeps its shape and Orion's belt stays three marks in a line. A number the phone cannot give (the Android row, as R38 left it) is a line marked open and is not a blocker.
- **D-742 — `v2.3.0` is `6cfa699`.** (V24-11; FR-STAR-9, Phase 2l's definition of done.) Nothing is tagged before `v2.5.0`, so wherever the spec measures against `v2.3.0` — the main chunk's size, the live page's and the pass detail's captures — the reference is the R110 merge, `6cfa699`, whose `package.json` reads 2.3.0. `scripts/bundle-budget.ts`'s rows and `captures.yml`'s `base` input name the SHA, never a tag. v2.5's `v2.4.0` is v2.4's release-preparation merge, by the same rule.
- **D-743 — The sources and the fixtures as they landed.** (FR-STAR-1, FR-STAR-2; V24-3, V24-12.) `data-src/stars/` holds `bsc5-catalog.gz` and `bsc5-ReadMe.txt` (the Yale catalogue as CDS V/50 ships it, 9110 records, 904 at V ≤ 4.5), `d3-celestial-constellations.lines.json` with its licence (89 features: Serpens is drawn as two), and `iau-csn.txt` (the WGSN names, joined to the catalogue by HD number), with a README carrying the sources, the licences and the SHA-256 of each file. `tests/docs/public.test.ts` counts `iau-csn.txt` as verbatim third-party text, because its header carries its maintainer's address. `tests/fixtures/stars/` holds one file per R1 site at one instant on 2026-11-01, each with twelve named stars (one per 30° of azimuth, at 12° or higher) and the five planets, beside a `.meta.json` naming the source. `astronomy-engine`'s one rotation is within 0.0065° of every value at capture, so the 0.25° tolerance has room and can still catch a wrong frame.

R111's decisions (2026-10-23, `docs/stars/FINDINGS.md`):

- **D-744 — The ref path, and V24-9 held.** (FR-STAR-9; V24-9.) The field's nodes are rendered once and each frame writes `x`, `y` and `visibility` to them outside React, as `spike/stars/Field.tsx`'s `RefField` does. Through React the field falls to 19 draws/s at 4× on the Pixel 5 profile; by ref it holds about 100 at 1×, 4× and 6×. On the owner's iPhone both paths draw at the sensor's 61 events/s. Glyphs cost what discs cost, so the stars stay characters.
- **D-745 — The catalogue as columns, and the budget at 40 KB.** (FR-STAR-1; OQ-39.) d3-celestial's figures, every endpoint snapped to a catalogue star (worst 0.0025°). 1035 stars (904 at V ≤ 4.5 and 131 fainter endpoints), 89 figures, 743 segments, 288 names: 21.1 KB gzipped as one array per field against 25.5 KB as objects. `STARS_BUDGET_KB` stays 40.
- **D-746 — Each glyph's ink centred on its point.** (FR-STAR-6.) In `--font-mono` the em box's centre is not the ink's: `.` draws 1.9–2.4 px low, `*` and `+` 0.6–0.9 px high, `@` centred, so figure lines stop short of their faint stars. Each glyph is shifted by its ink offset, measured once per glyph and size at load from the canvas's text metrics and applied as `dx`/`dy`. FR-STAR-6's centring wording is amended by v0.12's spec change.
- **D-747 — The ladder as written, and the picks for the second cut.** (FR-STAR-6.) The owner kept FR-STAR-6's 15/12 px, a collision distance of 0.5 of the small size and `.` for the faint steps; Crux and Orion's belt keep their shapes at 390 px. Two things go to v0.12 with the findings: the names layer needs a placement rule that avoids marks and lines and keeps each figure's name (the captures lose `Ori` to `Betelgeuse`), and the owner's four looks from Sky Guide — faint figure lines, spaced-capital figure names, the ground with N / E / S / W, and stronger brightness steps — each a spec change before a task.

Second cut (2026-10-23, SPEC v2.4.1, V24-13..V24-21), from `docs/stars/FINDINGS.md` and D-744..D-747:

- **D-748 — The catalogue is a committed build output, in columns, and the names are its data.** (FR-STAR-1, FR-STAR-10 as amended; V24-20, D-745.) `scripts/build-stars.ts` (`npm run build:stars`, run under `tsx`, never by `vite build`) reads `data-src/stars/` (D-743) and writes `src/data/stars/catalog.json`: one array per field — `ra` and `dec` (J2000 degrees, three decimals), `mag` (two), `name` (the IAU proper name or `""`), `desig` (Bayer or Flamsteed, or the HR number), `con` (the IAU abbreviation) — plus `figures`, one entry per drawn feature as `{ con, part, segments: [i, j][] }` with indices into the star arrays, every endpoint snapped to the nearest star as the spike did. It keeps every star at V ≤ `STAR_MAG_LIMIT` and every fainter endpoint, sorted by magnitude so the brightest come first. `src/data/stars/constellations.ts` is the Latin-name table, keyed by abbreviation, with `Ser` as two parts (`Serpens Caput`, `Serpens Cauda`) — the names are data, the same in both languages, and never enter the string catalog. `src/data/stars/catalog.ts` parses the file with `zod` once and returns typed arrays. The build prints the counts and the gzipped size; `tests/data/starCatalog.test.ts` pins 1035 stars, 89 features, 743 segments, every id in range and unique, every star name non-empty where present, the table complete for every `con` drawn, and the file ≤ 22 KB gzipped; it also re-runs the build into memory and asserts it equals the committed file, so the output cannot drift from its sources. The generated notices list packages only, so `scripts/third-party-notices.ts` gains a fixed `DATA_NOTICES` block written after them — d3-celestial's figures (BSD-3-Clause, its licence text from `data-src/stars/`), the Yale catalogue (public domain) and the IAU WGSN names — and `public/third-party-notices.txt` is regenerated.
- **D-749 — The positions in `lib/skyStars.ts`, and the budget row that follows the library.** (FR-STAR-2, FR-STAR-9; V24-5, V24-14.) `starsAt(catalog, observer, t)` returns, for one instant, `Float32Array`s of altitude and azimuth in catalogue order and the five planets as `{ body, azDeg, altDeg, mag }`: one `Rotation_EQJ_HOR(MakeTime(t), observer)` applied to every star's J2000 unit vector, the planets through `Equator` / `Horizon` (no refraction) and `Illumination(body, t).mag`. Memoised on `(t, lat, lon)` with one slot: a frame under the hand or the sensor reuses it, a change of `t` replaces it. The file joins `skyBodies.ts` as the lint boundary's second main-thread exception in `eslint.config.js`. It is imported only by the `stars` chunk. If Rollup then moves `astronomy-engine` out of `skyBodies-*.js` into a shared chunk, the `astronomy` row of `scripts/bundle-budget.ts` matches both files under its one limit, so the library is counted once, as now, and the row's total is what FR-STAR-9's "no other row moves" reads.
- **D-750 — `SkyScene` and `SkyCamera`, in the window's directory.** (FR-STAR-11, FR-STAR-4; V24-4.) `skychart/window/scene.ts` exports `SkyScene = { stars: StarField | null }` where `StarField` carries the catalogue, the positions of D-749 and the layer switches; everything else the scene names in the spec (horizon, rings, Sun, Moon, passes) stays where `SkyChartProps` carries it today, so no caller changes. `SkyChartProps` gains `scene?: SkyScene` and `namedStar?: number | null` with `onNameStar?(i: number | null)` (the list's and the tap's shared selection, FR-STAR-7) — the one shared file, `skychart/SkyChart.types.ts`. Absent `scene` is `v2.3.0`'s window, byte for byte. `skychart/window/camera.ts` holds `SkyCamera`: `source: 'sensor' | 'hand'`, the hand state `{ azDeg, altDeg }` with `dragTo`, `stepYaw`, `stepPitch`, `face(point)` and `up()`, clamped to `STARS_TILT_MIN_DEG`..`STARS_TILT_MAX_DEG`, composing `uprightRotation(az, alt)` (`projection.ts`); the three step constants are imported from `dome/camera.ts`, not moved. `useViewRotation(camera)` returns the one `Mat3` whichever source drives it, with `useDeviceOrientation` unchanged underneath. The window takes `camera?: SkyCamera`; without it the window is sensor-driven as now.
- **D-751 — One rotation channel; the star field reads it by ref.** (FR-STAR-9 as amended; D-744.) `useViewRotation` publishes each new rotation twice in the same animation frame: to React state, as today, for the window's existing layers, the readout, the ground state and the gutter (about twenty nodes, which React redraws within budget), and to a subscriber list. `skychart/window/StarField.tsx` is a `memo` child that renders its nodes once per catalogue and layer set — one `<text>` per star and planet, one `<line>` per segment, one `<text>` per name — and on each published rotation projects and writes `x`, `y`, `dx`, `dy` and `visibility` to them directly. Both writes land before the frame's paint, so the horizon and the stars never disagree. The label placement (D-755) runs only when the rotation has moved past `converged()` since the last placement, so names do not re-collide at the sensor's jitter.
- **D-752 — The ink offsets, measured once.** (FR-STAR-6 as amended; V24-15, D-746.) `skychart/window/inkOffsets.ts`: after `document.fonts.ready`, a canvas 2D context set to the window's computed `--font-mono` measures each glyph × size the ladder uses (`*` 18 and 15, `+` 12, `.` 12, `@` 18, 15 and 12) with `textAlign = 'center'` and `textBaseline = 'middle'`; the offset is the negated centre of `actualBoundingBox{Left,Right,Ascent,Descent}`, rounded to 0.1 px, cached in a module map. Where the canvas has no metrics (jsdom) every offset is 0, which is what the unit tests assume. The offsets are written as `dx`/`dy` when a node is created or its rung changes, never per frame.
- **D-753 — The ladder and the four tokens.** (FR-STAR-6, FR-DS-8 as amended; V24-13, V24-14.) `skychart/window/starGlyphs.ts` is the pure module: `rungFor(mag)` returns `{ glyph, sizeToken, colourToken }` on the five rungs of FR-STAR-6, planets on the same sizes with `@` and `--chart-planet`; `collide(points)` keeps the brighter of any two within half the small size; `hitTest(points, x, y)` returns the nearest within `--tap` / 4. `tokens.css` gains, in the type section, `--chart-text-18: 18px`; in the edges section, `--chart-hairline: calc(var(--hairline) * 0.75)`; in the colour section and the night block, `--chart-star-faint` (`#626d7a`, 3.65 : 1; night `#a24a40`, 3.51 : 1) and `--chart-figure-name` (`#7a8591`, 5.12 : 1; night `#c4544a`, 4.61 : 1). `scripts/contrast.ts` lists the faint star with `CHART_MARK_TOKENS` (≥ 3 : 1) and the figure name as text (≥ 4.5 : 1); `tests/styles/tokens.test.ts` also asserts each sits below `--chart-star-dim` in both themes; `docs/DESIGN.md` is regenerated.
- **D-754 — The figures' gap and clip, and the ground.** (FR-STAR-6 as amended; V24-13.) In `StarField`, a segment's two projected ends are each moved toward the other by the collision distance before writing; a segment whose projected length is under twice that is hidden. Segments with both ends below the horizon are hidden; the rest are drawn under a `clipPath` of the horizon's closed image (`groundClipPath`, the sky side, `clip-rule: evenodd` against the box) plus the field's edge. The ground is one `<path>` of the same closed image filled with `--chart-ground` at `--window-fill-opacity`, drawn when the scene carries stars and the horizon is in view, under the figures and under FR-FOL-5's hatch, whose two states are unchanged. The compass points are `SkyWindow`'s own `COMPASS` at `NAME_ALT_DEG`; nothing is added for them.
- **D-755 — The label placement.** (FR-STAR-6 as amended; V24-16.) `skychart/window/starLabels.ts`, pure: input the projected marks (point, glyph box from the rung), the drawn segments, the compass labels' boxes, the named mark, the star-name candidates (V ≤ 1.5, brightest first) and the figures (abbreviation, drawn endpoints); output the placed labels with their boxes. Text width is `n × 0.6 em` at the token's size, the spacing built into the string (`C R U X`, three spaces between words), so the boxes are the same in every engine. Occupied space is the mark boxes, the compass boxes and each segment sampled every 4 px. Order: compass (fixed), the named mark's label (right, left, above, below), star names (the same four), figure names (the full spaced name where its width ≤ the drawn endpoints' width + 2 cells, else the abbreviation; at the centroid, then one row above, then below; then the abbreviation in the same three). A figure name with no free place removes the placed star names it overlaps, faintest first, and is placed; a removed star name is not retried. A table test pins Orion over Paris (`O R I O N` and `Betelgeuse` both placed) and Crux over Neuquén. *(amended 2026-10-24, V24-22, D-778)* On R116's measure the six places cross the figure's own lines for both pinned figures, so after the centroid and the rows above and below it, each form searches a grid over the drawn endpoints' bounding box — one row (the name's 11 px) by one cell (0.6 em, 6.6 px), every place whose box reaches into the bounding box, nearest the centroid first — the full name's grid before the abbreviation's; the yielding step runs only when neither form found a free place, and walks the same list, so it takes the first place where only star names are in the way. The table test pins Orion over Paris (`O R I O N` at 390 and 1280, `Betelgeuse` at 1280 only, V24-23) and Crux over Neuquén (`C R U` at 390 and at 1280, where the cross is too narrow for the full name; `C R U X` in a 900 × 640 box).
