- **D-763 — The catalogue's columns as they landed.** (FR-STAR-1; D-748, D-745; R112.) The build prints 1033 stars (904 at V ≤ 4.5, 129 fainter endpoints) of 9096 positioned records, 89 features, 743 segments, worst snap 0.0025°, 289 names, 51.2 KB raw and 18.8 KB gzipped — under D-745's 21.1 KB because the positions are three decimals and the HR column is gone. A figure's point snaps to the nearest star by great-circle distance, searched in a declination band, and the build fails if any point sits farther than `SNAP_MAX_DEG` (0.1°); a tie, as on a double whose two Yale records share a position, goes to the brighter component — which keeps `Zet Boo`'s and `Alp Psc`'s fainter records out. A WGSN name whose record is not kept goes to the nearest kept star within `SNAP_MAX_DEG` that has no name of its own, so Alrescha, which the list gives the fainter `Alp Psc` record's HD, lands on the brighter one, and so does Izar (`Eps Boo`), which the first build missed; the build counts these carries and the test pins two. A segment the figure already draws, either way round, and one whose two points snap to one star are dropped (none are, today). When two WGSN lines carry one HD the first in the file keeps it and the build counts the rest (none, today); the test pins both counts at zero. Three details D-748 leaves open: a figure's `part` is its order among the features with the same abbreviation in d3-celestial's file, so Serpens' first feature (RA 233–240°) is part 0, `Serpens Caput`, and its second (RA 257–270°) part 1, `Serpens Cauda`; a Yale record names a constellation only beside a Bayer or Flamsteed designation, so for the 82 kept stars with neither, `con` is read off the IAU boundaries by `astronomy-engine`'s `Constellation()` at build time, which agrees with all 951 the catalogue does name; and `desig` is `Alp1 Cen` (letter, superscript, space, constellation) where the fixtures write `Alp1Cen`. `STAR_MAG_LIMIT` lives in `src/data/stars/constants.ts`, so the build reads it without loading the file it writes. `tests/data` joins `tsconfig.node.json`'s `include`, so the test is typechecked.
- **D-764 — A star's id is its index, and a designation is not unique.** (FR-STAR-1; D-748; R112.) The Yale catalogue lists the two components of six kept doubles as separate records with one designation (`Alp Gem`, `Zet Ori`, `Zet UMa`, `Gam Vir`, `Del Ser`, `Iot Cnc`), so "every id unique" is read as every star once: no two kept stars share designation, position and magnitude, and the duplicated designations are pinned at six. The label task decides how a reader tells the two apart.
- **D-765 — The data notices sit under their own rule.** (FR-STAR-1, FR-PUB-5; D-748; R112.) `public.test.ts` splits the notices file on `RULE` and holds the entries to the installed package tree, so `DATA_NOTICES` (`dataNotices()`) is written after the packages under `DATA_RULE` (76 `=`) with a `DATA` heading: d3-celestial's figures (BSD-3-Clause, quoted from `data-src/stars/d3-celestial-LICENSE.txt`), the Yale catalogue (public domain) and the IAU WGSN names (CC BY 4.0, the attribution its header asks for). `starCatalog.test.ts` holds the file to that list; `public.test.ts` cuts the file at the first `DATA_RULE` before it splits on `RULE`, so the data text never pads the last package's licence.
- **D-766 — The hand camera is a store the window drives and the page reads.** (R113; FR-STAR-4, FR-STAR-9; D-750.) `SkyCamera` is `SENSOR_CAMERA` (`{ source: 'sensor' }`, one value) or a `HandCamera` from `createHandCamera(initial)`: `get()`, `subscribe()`, and the five moves applied in place over the pure reducers `dragTo`, `stepYaw`, `stepPitch`, `face`, `up` (exported on their own for the test), each a normalised azimuth and a tilt clamped to `STARS_TILT_MIN_DEG`..`STARS_TILT_MAX_DEG`; a move that changes nothing notifies nobody. A store and not React state because the per-frame path under a drag must hold the window alone: `useViewRotation` reads it with `useSyncExternalStore`, the page (R115) reads the facing the same way for its picker and list, and no callback prop or parent re-render stands between a pointer move and the frame. `camera?` is on `SkyWindowProps` (`SkyChartProps & { camera? }`, exported by `SkyWindow.tsx`), not on `SkyChartProps`: the dome and the polar never see it, and the shared file carries only the three the scope names. The directions: a drag follows the finger, as the dome's does (right turns the azimuth down, down raises the altitude); `↑` looks up; `STARS_DEFAULT_FACING` is `{ north: 0, south: 180 }` with `defaultFacingDeg(lat)` and `initialHand(lat)` reading the hemisphere, since FR-STAR-3's default depends on the observer.
- **D-767 — The channel publishes in the layout effect of the commit that draws the rotation.** (R113; FR-STAR-9 as amended; D-751, D-744.) `useViewRotation(camera, declinationDeg, fallback)` returns the render's `Mat3` — the hand's `uprightRotation`, the sensor's, or the window's placeholder (`fallback`) before the first reading — and a `subscribe(listener)` whose listeners are called in a `useLayoutEffect` keyed on that `Mat3`, after React has written the commit's DOM and before the browser paints it. Not in the animation frame that set the state: React 19 commits a state set from an rAF in a later task, so a subscriber called there would place the stars a frame ahead of the horizon; in the layout effect the two writes are the same commit and no paint can fall between them. Exactly one call per rotation the window drew, none between commits, and a late subscriber is given the current rotation at once. `StarField` subscribes in its own layout effect, which runs before the parent's, so the first publish of its mount reaches it. R113's `StarField` is the empty `<g data-layer="stars">`, `memo`ed on `(field, view, subscribe)`, and its one write per rotation is the group's `visibility`, hidden at `buried`; it is mounted outside the `ground !== 'buried'` fragment so its nodes exist once across the ground states, and placed before the grid (under the horizon and the rings, FR-STAR-6).
- **D-768 — The sensor is not armed under the hand, and the hand's chrome is the one line.** (R113; FR-STAR-4, D-757.) `useDeviceOrientation(declinationDeg, enabled = true)` gains the one flag; `false` makes `available` false, so nothing is armed, no state moves and the handle reads as a device without the API — the sensor path's maths is untouched. Under a hand camera the window's `status` is the readout's first line (no declination line: the hand points at true bearings), there is no waiting note and no "hold the phone up" hint, the wrapper's `data-state` is `hand`, and the box is `tabIndex=0`, `aria-describedby` its readout, with the dome's `grab`/`grabbing` cursor and `touch-action: none`; the group's accessible name is the page's to add with its strings (R115). Under the sensor the box carries none of this, so its DOM is unchanged.
- **D-769 — What the dead-export check made of the new modules.** (R113; D-647.) `scene.ts` exports `StarField` and `SkyScene` alone; the parts (the catalogue's columns, the positions, a planet, the layer switches) are interfaces reached as `StarField['catalog']` until a task imports one by name, when it exports it. `drawField` is `StarField.tsx`'s private function until R114 fills it. `projection.ts`'s `projectDevice`, exported since R47 and imported by nothing (the spike has its own copy), is un-exported — it was the one report `npm run check:dead` made on the parent.
- **D-770 — Which side of the horizon's image is the sky depends on where the centre of the field is.** (R114; FR-STAR-6 as amended, FR-FOL-5; D-754, D-278.) `groundClipPath`'s closed curve is the stereographic image of the horizon, and the point at infinity is the antipode of the look direction: with the centre *above* the horizon the sky is the inside of the curve and the ground is everything outside it; *below* the horizon (FR-FOL-5's `ground` state, the only one R56 drew it in) the sides swap. So D-754's "the sky side, `evenodd` against the box" is one of two paths per frame, chosen by the sign of `lookDirection(rotation).altDeg`: the sky-side clip is the image alone when the centre is up and the box's rectangle plus the image under `clip-rule: evenodd` when it is down, and the ground fill is the other of the two under `fill-rule: evenodd`. Nothing tests "the horizon is in view" separately: when it is out of the box the image encloses the box and the floor's `evenodd` path covers nothing inside it, and at `buried` the whole group is hidden as R113 left it. `SkyWindow.stars.test.tsx` holds the three states with R56's point-in-polygon reader, and that the image the field fills at `ground` is byte for byte the one the window clips its hatch to.
- **D-771 — The ink offsets probe is the browser project's test, and the numbers on the Mac.** (R114; FR-STAR-6 as amended, V24-15; D-752.) The brief asked for an e2e probe of `inkOffsets.ts` on any page; a Playwright spec cannot import the module into the page, so it would have carried a copy of the measurement. `inkOffsets.integration.test.ts` instead runs in `vitest.config.ts`'s `browser` project (`src/**/*.integration.test.ts`, real Chromium), imports the module and the sheet, prints the table and holds its shape — `.` below the point, `*` and `+` at or above it, `@` within 1.5 px, nothing past 4 px, every value a tenth — without pinning values that are the machine's face's. The `ui` project collects every test under `src/ui` into jsdom as well, so the file `describe.skipIf`s itself where `document.fonts` is missing. Measured on the owner's Mac (`ui-monospace` resolves to SF Mono): `*` 18 px dx 0.0 dy +0.9; `*` 15 px 0.0/+0.7; `+` 12 px −0.1/+0.7; `.` 12 px +0.3/−1.9; `@` 18/15/12 px +0.1/0.0 — the spike's figures (`docs/stars/FINDINGS.md` §5) to the tenth. `dx`/`dy` are rendered as attributes from the module's map (0 before the measurement), and a field mounted before the fonts are ready writes them once more when `inkOffsetsReady()` resolves; a field mounted after it has them from its render and skips the pass.
- **D-772 — The frame's walk: one projection per star, the planets in the magnitude order, a margin for the edge.** (R114; FR-STAR-6 as amended, FR-STAR-9.) Per published rotation `StarField` projects every catalogue star once into four typed arrays (`x`, `y`, off-axis angle, in front) — the glyphs need the ones up and in the box, the segments need both ends whatever they are — and the planets separately. The collision walk is `collide` over the stars and the planets *together* in magnitude order (`prepare()` sorts the combined index once per field), so a planet fainter than a star beside it is the one dropped, where the spike always kept the planet. A glyph is drawn while its centre is within half the top size (9 px) of the box, so an 18 px `*` leaves the frame rather than winking out at its edge; a segment's ends are projected to `drawableDeg` plus 15°, the spike's margin, so a line to a star just outside the frame reaches the edge. A layer that is off skips its loop (its group is hidden by the render), so the three switches cost nothing per frame; the nodes stay, and a switch re-renders the field once and re-subscribes, which replays the current rotation.
- **D-773 — What else R114 settled in the window's files.** (R114; FR-DS-2, D-647, D-753.) `starGlyphs.ts` carries the two px numbers the rules need — `SIZE_PX`, the three chart text tokens' values under their names, and `HIT_RADIUS_PX`, `--tap` / 4 — and `starGlyphs.test.ts` reads `tokens.css` and holds both to it, `gutter.test.ts`'s pattern for `GUTTER_PX`; the stylesheet names every size and tone by token (`.size18 { font-size: var(--chart-text-18) }`, `.starFaint { fill: var(--chart-star-faint) }`, `.figures line { stroke-width: var(--chart-hairline) }`), so `literals.allow.json` gains nothing. `SkyPoint`, `ring`, `HORIZON` and `groundClipPath` move from `SkyWindow.tsx` to `projection.ts`, exported, because the field projects the same 181 horizon points per frame that the window projects per render (F-57's one sampling, two readers). `hitTest` is exported with no caller but its test, for R116's tap. The scene's `StarFigure.segments` is pairs (`readonly [number, number][]`, D-750) while `data/stars/catalog.ts` stores a flat `Uint16Array`: the page maps the catalogue into the scene's shape once per load, or R115 proposes the one type; R114 keeps the scene as R113 cut it. `scripts/contrast.ts`'s `CHART_RESERVED_TOKENS` keeps its name and gains `chart-star-faint`: the dome's palette test (`dome/palette.test.tsx`, outside the lane) reads it as the chart marks that are not the dome's, and the five star marks are the window's now, not reserved; the guide's cell keeps its "reserved for the stars" phrase because `tests/docs/design.test.ts` (also outside the lane) pins it.
- **D-774 — `[ stars ]` on the wide title row moves the header's fold, and the live link folds with the title.** (R115; FR-STAR-3, FR-HOME-1; D-546, D-605, F-76.) The title row gains two cells and `[ stars ]` / `[ estrellas ]`: 112 cells in English and 128 in Spanish, so `HEADER_FOLD_PX.*.title` is 1079 and 1233 px (`thresholdPx`), `Header.module.css`'s two folds with it and `tests/styles/breakpoints.json`. The short title alone would leave the Spanish row at 105 cells, over the wide breakpoint's 100, so under the same fold `[ Cielo en vivo ]` takes its short word (`live.openShort`, drawn from a `data-short` attribute as the title's is): 87 and 96 cells folded. F-76's reading moves: both languages are under their fold at 1024 px and Spanish at the three panes too; neither is at 1280. `controlRows.test.ts` and `home-desk.spec.ts` assert the new arithmetic, and `breakpoint.test.ts` holds the title folds under `WIDE_SPLIT_MIN_PX` instead of the three panes'. On the stars page the header's title is a `p`, so the page's own name is the route's one `h1` (FR-A11Y-1), as on the live page.
- **D-775 — `src/ui` may import `src/data/stars`.** (R115; D-756, PLAN §3.) D-756 has the page build its scene from `catalog.ts`, and §3's zone forbids `src/ui` → `src/data`; `eslint.config.js`'s zone gains `./stars` as its one exception, beside the comment that names D-756. The only importer is the `stars` chunk (`Stars.tsx`, `stars/field.ts`), so the catalogue stays out of main. The catalogue's figures are flat index pairs with a numeric part, the window's scene types pairs with a word (`Caput`, `Cauda`); the page converts once (`sceneCatalog`, memoised on the catalogue), the one place both shapes meet.
- **D-776 — The page's layout as built.** (R115; FR-STAR-3, FR-COMP-4, FR-COMP-5, FR-LIVE-7.) The window is placed, not restyled: the page leaves `SkyWindow` untouched and puts its frame's cells by `Stars.module.css` through the frame's test ids and the `data-row="controls"` / `data-row="status"` names `ChartFrame` gives its two rows (review fix: never by child order) — the empty controls row not drawn, the status slot (the window's own readout) the row above the box on compact and an overlay in the box's top-left corner on wide, on the screen overlay's surface. **Wide:** the box is cut by `fitBox` to the browser window's own aspect ("the window's shape") from the page's height and the width beside a rail of `RAIL_MIN_CELLS`, the rail taking the rest up to 60 cells and scrolling inside; the page does not scroll. **Compact:** the readout row, the box full-bleed and square (390 × 390 at 390 × 844, so FR-COMP-5's floor holds), the facing row, the layers, the list; the page scrolls past the box. The facing picker is a `ToggleGroup` in the compact speeds' tight form (D-245) with a cell between the options, `N NE E SE [S] SW W NW up`, 24 cells in English and 28 in Spanish — the bracketed form reserves `[ ` ` ]` on every option and is 58; a point keeps the current tilt (FR-STAR-4), so from the zenith `up` stays pressed; after a drag no point is pressed. The layers are four `OptionToggle`s in two rows of two on every width — one row of four is 43 cells in English and 51 in Spanish — and FR-STAR-3's "the layers row" is read as the two. The h2 headings `Facing` and `Layers` are visually hidden on compact, where the rows are their own label. The page's focus target is the drawing's box, focused on mount (it takes the arrow keys); the box is wrapped in a `group` named by the page. The list reads the camera through `useDeferredValue`, so a drag's frame is the window's alone; a row's focus or click names its mark (`namedStar` held by the page, cleared after `STAR_LABEL_HOLD_S`, a new naming restarting the hold), and the window's `onNameStar(null)` clears it. The `[ stars ]` link and the When pane's `[ look up ]` prefetch the chunk on `pointerenter` and `focus`; there is no idle prefetch, since the chunk is some 24 KB and a reader who never opens the page should not pay it on a phone. The When pane's line is set at `--small` (Spanish 38 of 41 characters).
- **D-777 — The page's own words ride in the `stars` chunk.** (R115; FR-STAR-9, FR-STAR-10, FR-I18N-2; D-69, D-756.) D-756's one `stars` section in both catalogs measured main at +1.3 KB over `6cfa699`, over FR-STAR-9's 1 KB: the two languages' page words are 0.76 KB gzipped on their own. The section is split by who draws the word. `i18n/{en,es}/stars.ts`, merged into the catalogs, holds what main draws — the header's link, the page's name and title, the When pane's line, the loading line, the `?` overlay's block — and `i18n/{en,es}/starsPage.ts` holds the rest — the inert line, the drawing's name, the three blocks, the picker's `up`, the layer names, the list's words and the planets' names, `mag`, the readout's form and the named line, and R117's `[ hold up to the sky ]` — read by `useStarsPageT()` in the active language and imported only from the chunk (and, for R116, the window it renders). `es/starsPage.ts` is typed `typeof` the English, so a missing word is still a `tsc -b` failure (FR-I18N-2). Main measures +923 bytes. The magnitude prints one decimal, the typographic minus and no plus (`mag 0.6`, `mag −0.7`, `mag 1,3`), the page's `formatStarMag`, since the pass card's `formatMagnitude` signs both ways.
- **D-778 — The figure name's grid.** (R116; FR-STAR-6 as amended, V24-22; D-755.) `placeLabels` keeps D-755's three places, then `gridOffsets` walks the offsets `(i × cell, j × row)` whose point lies inside the drawn endpoints' bounding box grown by half the name's box (so the box reaches into it: Crux at 390 is 23 × 36 px, narrower than `C R U`), sorted by distance from the centroid (ties by row, then column, so the order is fixed), the three places left out; the full spaced name's places, then the abbreviation's. The yielding step walks that same list, not the three places alone: a pinned figure's three places all cross its own lines, which never yield, and with the yielding step on them alone `C R U` was still lost to `Acrux` and `Mimosa`. Measured on the catalogue with the camera on the figure's mean direction: Orion over Paris (2026-12-15T23:00Z) places `O R I O N` at 390 × 390 and at 798 × 498 (the box the page draws at 1280 × 800), Crux over Neuquén (2027-04-15T03:00Z) `C R U` at both and `C R U X` in a 900 × 640 box, and the sky cases' invariant — no label on a mark, a segment sample or another label — holds. The grid is clipped to the places whose box fits the field (a large figure's up-sky ends can project thousands of px out) and walked lazily, stopping at the first free place, so a figure whose centroid is free costs three queries; the placement runs only past `converged()` or when the drawn set changes.
- **D-779 — `Betelgeuse` at 390 is dropped, and the Done is read that way.** (R116; FR-STAR-6, FR-STAR-7, V24-23.) At 60° across 390 px the four places beside Betelgeuse each cover a mark or one of Orion's four lines that meet at it; eight directions at four distances (to 36 px) were no better. The rule stays: no star name covers a mark or a line, and a dropped name is a tap away. R116's `Done when` names `Betelgeuse` placed at 1280 only; the test pins it at 798 × 498, the box the page draws at 1280 × 800, and at 390 pins only that it is not placed over anything.
- **D-780 — The window row stays over until the release.** (R116; FR-STAR-9, V24-24; D-759, D-178.) `window` measures 21.8 KB on this branch, rebased on R117 (budget 15; 16.8 on `main` before R116), `stars` 23.6 (40), `main` 169.7 (170). The overrun is the budget script's `::warning::`, not a failure. Handing the words to the window in the scene would move `Stars.tsx`, outside the `window` lane, under the deadline; the owner chose the re-set at R118 by D-178's rule, D-759 amended to say so.
- **D-781 — What R116 settled in the placement.** (R116; FR-STAR-6 as amended, FR-STAR-7; D-755.) Accepted by the owner as written: a mark's box is its glyph's cell, 0.6 em square, centred on the ink; the gap between a mark and its name is half a cell at the name's size; a row is the name's own height; figures are named in order of most drawn segments first; the named label is never dropped — with no free place it takes the first of its four places that is inside the box; it is drawn in `--chart-star-dim` at `--chart-text-12`, like a star's name; and the tap and the hover are wired for the hand camera only, the sensor screen's tap being R117's. Settled at the review: where a tap can name, the hand camera holds still until the press travels past the hit radius (12 px), and the tap is tested at the press point, so a finger's wobble neither turns the sky nor misses the mark; a mouse drag clears the hover; a star named from `In this field` whose glyph the collision hid is labelled at its own point; the compass boxes follow the window's own in-view rule (`EDGE_MARGIN_PX`, now `projection.ts`'s).
- **D-782 — The stars inventory takes the scene as a prop, and `open()` keeps its signature.** (R117; FR-STAR-5, FR-FSC-8; D-756.) D-756 says `useSkyScreen.open()` takes the scene. A scene handed over at the tap would be the instant of the tap, and FR-FSC-8 has the screen show the page's instant as it runs; the hook's state is the store's flag, which a page reads to render the layer over itself (D-350). So the tap stays `open()`, and `SkyScreen`'s props are a union on `inventory`: `'passes'` (the default, unchanged) or `'stars'` with the page's live `scene` and no `passes`. `Stars.tsx` portals the layer to the body as the pass detail does, closes it on `Esc` in the capture phase (the app's `Esc` would leave `#stars`) and on unmount, holds the document's scroll under it (FR-FSC-9: the compact page scrolls the document), and gives the document its place and the focus back to `[ hold up to the sky ]` on a close of the screen it opened — not on the store's global `refocusWindow`, which a close on any page sets, and not on an unmount (a route change). Under the layer the page is `inert` and `aria-hidden` and held at its last render, so a tick redraws one window, the screen's. `FR-LIVE-8`'s note shows only after this page's own tap. The screen is the sensor's, so it gets no `camera`; it starts at the hand's azimuth at the open (`initialFacingAzDeg`).
- **D-783 — What the window builds for a screen with no pass is left out by the layer.** (R117; FR-FSC-1 as amended v2.4, FR-GUT-6, FR-GUT-7.) The task said the window already draws no chip without a pass. It does draw one — `t.window.emptySky`, "no pass to turn to" — on any screen with an instant and nothing in the field; upright it draws the next-event block; and `SkyChart` builds a legend of the Sun and Moon lines. So `SkyChartProps` carries the inventory (`inventory: 'stars'`, from `SkyScreen`): `SkyChart` builds no legend and the window no chip and no next-event block; FR-FSC-11's advice line under the block stays. Hiding them by test id in CSS (the first cut) still built them every tick and would have come back on a renamed id.
- **D-784 — `[ hold up to the sky ]` stands after the layers in both layouts.** (R117; FR-STAR-3, FR-STAR-5, FR-WIN-4.) FR-STAR-3 places the row on compact; a wide touch device (a tablet held sideways) passes the presence test too, so the row is in the rail under `Layers` there, and on a desk it is not rendered. FR-LIVE-8's note stands beside it (`role="status"`, the one part of the row that wraps); a relative-only phone loses the control for the session (`windowLost`) and keeps the note, as the view control does.
- **D-785 — The release re-sets `stars` to 30 and `window` to 25.** (R118; FR-STAR-9, V24-24; D-178, D-759 as amended, D-780.) On the 2.4.0 build, gzip level 9: `stars` 23.6 KB, × 1.1 = 26.0, the next 5 KB line 30, under `STARS_BUDGET_KB` (40), which stays the ceiling; `window` 22.1, × 1.1 = 24.3, so 25 (no ceiling in §11, as since D-242). The reason for the window's size is written beside its row in `scripts/bundle-budget.ts`: the names, the page's label words, the constellation table and the magnitude format are shared with the `stars` chunk and Rollup puts what two chunks share in `SkyWindow-*.js`. Every other row is the rule agreeing with the number already there. The table, beside `6cfa699`'s built on the same machine, is `docs/RELEASE.md` §16.2 and the comment at the top of the script.
- **D-786 — The capture set gains `stars` at 360, 390, 1280 and 1920 and `stars-screen` at 844, and touch is a property of the capture.** (R118; FR-CAP-1, FR-CAP-2, FR-STAR-3, FR-STAR-5; D-758.) D-758 names the page at 390, 1280 and 1920; FR-CAP-2 puts a 360 px file beside every compact 390, and `captures.test.ts` holds every non-sky-screen to it, so the page has four widths (16 files). The screen is `stars-screen` so its files are `v1-stars-*` as the entry asks, and it joins the sky screen's exception in `captures.test.ts` (844 only). The page is shot on a touch phone at 360 and 390, where `[ hold up to the sky ]` is on it, and on a desk without touch at 1280 and 1920, where FR-WIN-4 leaves it off — so `v1-captures.spec.ts` decides touch per capture (`isTouch`) rather than per screen. Both are reached through the home with the list settled, like the live page, so the background run cannot change the document between `settled`'s two ticks; the page faces south 35° up as it opens, and the screen is aimed there. The set is 274 files. The shortcuts route counted the overlay's 8 keys and had failed since R115 added `s` and the page's two rows; it counts 11.
- **D-787 — The diff against `6cfa699` is measured locally, and main's 0.24 KB is recorded, not trimmed.** (R118; FR-CAP-5, FR-STAR-9, V24-11; D-742.) A task session cannot dispatch `captures.yml`, and the committed set is the Linux renderer's (D-732), so a Mac run against it differs everywhere. The diff of record for the task is both commits shot on one Mac by this branch's spec off plain builds: 155 of 254 byte-identical, 99 differing, every one on four lists — the header's `[ stars ]` (48), the When pane's line (24), the `?` overlay's three new keys (12), F-99's noise (15). The entry's "none changed" is read as "nothing but what the phase's own requirements moved". The review dispatched `captures.yml` on the branch (runs 40106274669 and 40106522515, D-732's Linux renderer), and run 1's artefact is the committed set in place of the Mac's 20 files (`docs/RELEASE.md` §16.1). Main is 1,270 bytes over `6cfa699` against FR-STAR-9's 1 KB; with no `src/` in this task the figure goes to the owner (`docs/RELEASE.md` §16.4), as v2.3's did (D-738).


### 2.40 v2.5 decisions (2026-10-25)

SPEC v2.5 moves the satellites onto the scene v2.4 built for the stars. The work is mostly plumbing that must change nothing (one scene, one table) and three hand-camera behaviours that must feel right (the box, the following key, the zoom); the decisions below fix the plumbing so the camera tasks spend their effort where the drawing is. The owner's design canvas (V25-12, https://claude.ai/artifact/MJkqMq4RzHrpXd7eo7yJmN) is the reference for every new control and line: a task matches its board's copy, order and spacing, translated into the sheet's tokens and the primitives by the names `docs/DESIGN.md` prints (FR-DS-9); the canvas's sky is illustrative and is not a fixture.

- **D-788 — One scene hook, one pure table, and the passes stay on their path.** (FR-SKY-1, FR-LIVE-10 as amended; V25-2; D-750.) `skychart/useSkyScene.ts` builds `SkyScene` once per tick from the observer, the shown instant and the prefs, memoised on `(observer, t, starsLayer, sunAltDeg)`, and is called once per page — the live page, the pass detail, the stars page — never per view, so a page with two drawings (the Where pane's dome and the screen) shares one. `skychart/layers.ts` exports `LAYERS: Record<'dome' | 'polar' | 'window', readonly Layer[]>` with `Layer = 'passes' | 'bodies' | 'stars' | 'figures' | 'planets' | 'names' | 'landmark'`, `POLAR_STAR_MAG` (3.5) and `DOME_STAR_MAG` (1.5), and `drawsLayer(view, layer)`; a view filters the scene through it and has no condition of its own. The Where pane's dome passes a scene with `stars: null` (OQ-44). `SkyChartProps.scene` stays optional; without it a view draws `ece8bfd`'s picture, which is what the contract test's old cases keep proving while its star case proves the anchors. No visible change: the task's proof is the capture set byte-identical against `ece8bfd` for every file it re-shoots.
- **D-789 — The window is offered everywhere, laid out in the box from what the frame measures.** (FR-SKY-2, FR-WIN-4, FR-WIN-5, FR-FSC-6 as amended; V25-1, V25-3; D-188, D-352.) `SKY_CHART_VIEWS`' `WINDOW_VIEW.available()` returns true; the presence test moves to the one question it still answers, whether the screen can follow (D-175's test, read by `useSkyScreen`). `ChartFrame` gains the window's box — the box it already measures, cut to the window's shape as `Stars.tsx` cuts its own (one `windowBox(measured)` beside `fitBox`, shared by both) — so the wide live page and pass detail lay the window out where the dome sits, with the readout in the box's top-left corner and the hand hint in its bottom-left, as the canvas draws them. The hand camera is `createHandCamera` (D-750) on both pages, its state held by the page so a view change and back keeps the facing. `model/prefs.ts`'s `chartView` admits `'window'`; `localPrefs.ts`'s load narrows it to the dome below `layout.ts`'s wide breakpoint, and a compact choice of the window without a sensor is page state and never written. The tablet's `[ hold up to the sky ]` in the rail is `useSkyScreen.open()`, unchanged.
- **D-790 — The pass detail opens on the peak.** (FR-SKY-7; V25-8.) `camera.ts` gains `facePeak(state, peak, fovDeg)` → facing `peak.az`, tilt `clamp(peak.alt − 15, 20, 75)`, and the pass detail's `initialHand` is it; the facing picker takes an option list from its page, and the pass detail's list is `['peak', ...COMPASS_POINTS, 'up']`. On the screen the sensor's first reading replaces it (FR-FSC-10).
- **D-791 — `starsLayer`, the toggle, the chunk, and the twilight steps as one function.** (FR-SKY-3, FR-SKY-8, FR-SKY-10, FR-STAR-13 as amended; V25-4.) `model/prefs.ts` and `state/slices/prefs.ts` gain `starsLayer: boolean`, default true, persisted by `localPrefs.ts` with its schema test; the toggle is `OptionToggle` on the live page's actions row and the pass detail's view row (compact: the readout row, as the canvas's 390 px board). With it on, the page imports `starsChunk.ts` (the chunk R115 cut) when it mounts and, with it off, prefetches it with `requestIdleCallback` after its own chunk so turning it on draws on the next tick; while the chunk is loading the views draw without stars. `lib/skyStars.ts` gains `drawnRungs(sunAltDeg): 0 | 2 | 5` and `planetsDrawn(sunAltDeg)` reading the −6° step from `VisibilityThresholds.sunAltMaxDeg` (the threshold `skyStateOf` already uses, so the stars thin exactly when the page says the sky is bright) and the 0° step as `DAYLIGHT_ALT` beside it, and every view's star group reads them through the scene: one rule thins the stars page, its screen and the pass pages. The rotation is one per shown instant (FR-SKY-8): the scene's positions are memoised on `t`, so playback at 3600× recomputes once per frame and never per view.
- **D-792 — The polar chart's stars are a group on V24-9's glyphs.** (FR-SKY-4, FR-SKY-10; V25-6.) `SkyPolar.tsx` gains one `<g>` under the arcs drawing the scene's stars to `POLAR_STAR_MAG` with `starGlyphs.ts`'s ladder scaled by the chart's unit as its labels are, the planets as `@`; it follows the looking-up / map toggle with the arcs. `starGlyphs.ts` moves no file; Vite places it in a shared chunk charged to `main` (≤ 1 KB with the toggle and the prefetch). `SkyPolar.live.svg` is re-baselined once, by this task.
- **D-793 — The dome's stars are one points mesh in the line layer, and the rate is measured.** (FR-SKY-5, FR-DOME-7 as amended; V25-5.) `domeLayers.ts` gains one mesh of single braille dots for the scene's stars to `DOME_STAR_MAG` and the planets, coloured through `palette.ts`'s two new entries (`--chart-star`, `--chart-planet`), under the line layer's arcs; no figure, no name. `dome-perf.spec.ts` measures the drag rate with the stars on against a constant measured on `ece8bfd` by the same spec and committed beside the existing ones (the task's first commit), and fails below 0.9 × that or below 30. The raster snapshots (`SkyDome.golden.txt`, `SkyDome.live.txt`) are re-baselined once, by this task. If the mesh cannot hold the rate the task stops and reports, rather than thinning the twenty: the cap is the spec's.
- **D-794 — One screen; the inventory names only the way back.** (FR-SKY-6, FR-FSC-1 as amended; V25-4; D-756, D-782.) `SkyScreen` keeps `inventory: 'passes' | 'stars'` for the return route and the `×` only; the gutter's ticks and chip read `scene`'s passes, so the stars page's screen draws them whenever `[ passes ]` put them in the scene. The stars page's `[ passes ]` is page state, off, never saved; with it on the page asks the store for FR-TRAJ-1's set at now and passes it with the scene, and `screens/stars/field.ts` gains pass rows (key, name, FR-LEG-3's state word, peak altitude and direction) ahead of the stars, as the canvas's stars board lists them.
- **D-795 — The landmark, the constellation at a point and the figure's hit are pure functions in the `data` lane.** (FR-SKY-11, FR-SKY-12, FR-STAR-14; V25-9, V25-10, V25-13.) `src/lib/landmark.ts`: `landmark(stars, peak, rungs)` → `{ index, sepDeg, word: 'above' | 'below' | 'beside' } | null` with `LANDMARK_MAG` 2.5, `LANDMARK_DEG` 12° and `LANDMARK_LEVEL_DEG` 2°, picking only among stars `drawnRungs` draws, never a planet; `constellationAt(altAz, figures)` → the figure whose drawn segments come nearest by great-circle distance within `AMONG_MAX_DEG` 10°, else null; `segmentDistanceDeg` exported for FR-STAR-14's tap. All three take the positions `skyStars.ts` already produces and run in the `stars` chunk (FR-SKY-10 as amended: ≤ 1 KB on the row). Tested against the three fixture sites (`tests/fixtures/stars/`) and hand cases for every branch.
- **D-796 — The line, the ring, the name and the column.** (FR-SKY-11, FR-SKY-12, FR-LEG-1 as amended.) `SkyScene` gains `landmark` (computed by `useSkyScene` for the highlighted pass through D-795); `LAYERS` gives the ring to every view and the name to the window only, the screen being a window. The ring is `LANDMARK_RING_PX` (13 px) dashed in `--chart-star`; in the dome it is drawn only when the landmark is one of the dome's own stars. The name is placed by `starLabels.ts`'s placement as any tapped star's is, and a tap's label takes its place while it holds. The line under the pass's name is one formatter in `lib/landmarkLine.ts` (`ui` lane, beside the pass-path formatter) used by the live page's headline block, the pass detail's head and the screen's readout second line. The pass detail's table gains the `Among` / `Entre` column from `constellationAt` at each point; Latin names in both languages (V25-10).
- **D-797 — The facing key follows the pass.** (FR-SKY-13, FR-DESK-4 as amended; V25-11.) The facing picker's option type becomes `CompassPoint | 'up' | 'peak' | { pass: string }`; `HandState` gains `follow: string | null`; `followPass(state, altAz, fovDeg)` re-aims at `clamp(alt − 15, 20, 75)` and is applied by the page on every tick while `follow` is set, before the frame is drawn; `dragTo`, `stepYaw`, `stepPitch` and `face` clear it. The pass is the highlighted one; its position is the live marker's, its rise or set point outside its window. `lib/shortcuts.ts` gains `f` on the live page only. The readout's first line reads `Following A` while it holds.
- **D-798 — Zoom is the camera's `fovDeg`.** (FR-SKY-14, FR-WIN-1, FR-GUT-3, FR-STAR-4 as amended; V25-14; D-204, D-285.) `projection.ts`'s `View` already carries `fovDeg`; every caller that passes `WINDOW_FOV` today (`Stars.tsx`, `SkyWindow.tsx`, `gutter.ts`, the ground state) passes the camera's instead. `HandState` and the screen's sensor state gain `fovDeg`, default `WINDOW_FOV`; `zoomBy(state, factor)` clamps to `WINDOW_FOV_MIN_DEG` 20 and `WINDOW_FOV_MAX_DEG` 90, constants beside `WINDOW_FOV`. One pointer handler on the box (window lane) tracks active pointers: one is FR-STAR-4's drag, two are the pinch (the ratio of distances per frame, about the centre); a `wheel` listener registered with `passive: false` calls `preventDefault()` only when `ctrlKey` is set and scales by `exp(deltaY × ZOOM_WHEEL_RATE)`; `+`/`=`/`-`/`0` are the box's keys beside the arrows. `fovDeg` lives in page state and is never written to the prefs or the hash. The readout's suffix is ` · field 30°`. Glyph sizes, hit and collision distances are px constants already and stay so.
- **D-799 — The tests, the captures and the budgets.** (FR-SKY-9, FR-SKY-10; V25-7; D-178.) Each task lists its tests in §9.7; the capture set (`tests/e2e/captureSet.ts`) gains, in the release preparation, the files FR-SKY-9 names, and every re-shot file of an earlier task is byte-identical to `ece8bfd` except that task's named moves, which its `Done` lists by file. `npm run bundle:budget` is run by every task and the table is in its PR; the rows move only as FR-SKY-10 allows (`chart` ≤ 2 KB, `main` ≤ 1 KB, `live` ≤ 1 KB, `stars` ≤ 1 KB for D-795, `window` for D-797 and D-798 within its 25 KB row); the release re-sets every row by D-178.
- **D-800 — Every task is `Gate: auto`, the release preparation included.** (V25-15, V24-21, V24-11; D-760.) As v2.4's second cut: a task merges on CI green and a clean `opus` review, the visual ones, the Spanish copy and the release preparation included; every choice a task would otherwise bring to the owner is taken in SPEC v2.5 and here, and the canvas is the visual reference. The owner's look is read at the release preparation and blocks only the tag: the capture set in both themes, one pass watched through the phone with the stars on, one scrubbed at a desk in the window. The `v2.5.0` tag, the push to `release` and the deploy are the owner's (RELEASE §17).
- **D-801 — The sessions: `fable` where the drawing must be iterated, `opus` elsewhere.** (V25-15; §16.6, D-761.) D-761's test, applied again: `fable` implements the five tasks where a plausible wrong answer is expensive and the session must iterate against what it draws or measures — the scene and the table (every view's picture must stay byte-identical while the plumbing under it changes), the window in the box on two pages (the fit geometry that F-60 and F-61 showed is easy to get subtly wrong), the dome's points mesh against the rate, the zoom's pointer handling, and the landmark's ring and name with the following camera; `opus` implements the pure functions, the polar group, the strings and toggle, the one screen and the release, which the tables and tests specify fully. `opus` reviews every task; `Turns: 500` and `Fallback: off` on every row. Sonnet is not used: with no owner gate (D-800), a cheaper implementer's miss in copy or spacing lands on `main` with only the review between it and the release, and D-761 kept the same line for the same reason; the saving would be in the five `opus` tasks, which are the cheap ones already.
- **D-805 — The pure functions take the catalogue and the positions as arguments.** (R120; FR-SKY-11, FR-SKY-12, FR-STAR-10 as amended; D-795, D-832.) The lint boundary keeps `src/lib` from importing `src/data` (PLAN §3, `eslint.config.js`), so D-832's `starName(i, lang)`, `figureName(con, part, lang)` and `constellationName(con, lang)` take the catalogue first, as `starsAt` does: `starName(catalog, i, lang)` and so on, typed by `StarNamesSource`. `StarCatalog` gains `nameEs` and `figureNames` / `wholeNames` keyed by language: the English tables are `constellations.ts`'s (`CONSTELLATION_NAMES`, and `CONSTELLATION_WHOLE_NAMES = { Ser: 'Serpens' }`, new), the Spanish ones `catalog.json`'s `figuresEs` and `wholeEs`, so a caller reaches every name through the three readers. D-795's `landmark(stars, peak, rungs)` takes `stars` as `{ mag, altDeg, azDeg }` (the catalogue's magnitudes beside `starsAt`'s positions), and `constellationAt(point, figures, positions)` takes the positions third and returns `{ con, part, deg }`, the caller naming `con` through `constellationName` (Serpens' halves one name). `constellations.ts`'s own English-only `figureName(con, part)` is removed, so an auto-import cannot pick it: its one `src/ui` caller (`field.ts`'s `sceneCatalog`) reads `figureName(catalog, con, part, 'en')`, the same string; R126 and R127 move the rest of `src/ui` onto the readers.
- **D-806 — `drawnRungs` counts the ladder's five rungs, and the landmark is drawn or nothing.** (R120; FR-STAR-13, FR-SKY-3, FR-SKY-11; D-791, D-795.) `drawnRungs(sunAltDeg, thresholds?)` is in `skyStars.ts`, where D-791 puts it and where the physics constant may be read (the lint exception), and `landmark.ts` re-exports it, as the task entry lists it there. It returns how many of FR-STAR-6's rungs are drawn: `RUNG_MAX_MAG.length` (5) at `sunAltMaxDeg` (−6°) and below, 2 up to `DAYLIGHT_ALT` (0°), 0 above, and 0 for a Sun altitude that is not a number, as `planetsDrawn` is false then; the return type is the literal `0 | 2 | 5`. D-791 first read `0 | 2 | 3`, a slip the owner confirmed on 2026-10-26 (it now reads `0 | 2 | 5`), the ladder (`starGlyphs.ts`'s `LADDER`) having five rows, and `LADDER` takes its bounds from `RUNG_MAX_MAG`, which lives in `src/lib/starRungs.ts`, a module with no imports, so the window's chunk reads it without `skyStars.ts`'s ephemeris. `planetsDrawn` and `drawnMagLimit(rungs)` sit beside it. The landmark's candidates are also above the horizon — FR-STAR-6 draws nothing below it, and FR-SKY-11 picks among the stars drawn — and a tie goes to the brighter, the catalogue's order.
- **D-807 — The Spanish names cost the `stars` chunk 1,007 bytes.** (R120; FR-SKY-10 as amended v2.5; D-832.) Built against `ece8bfd`'s four star files on the same machine, the `Stars-*.js` chunk goes from 24,168 to 25,175 bytes gzipped (level 9), inside FR-SKY-10's ≤ 1 KB for the names and over D-832's estimate of 0.7 KB; `main` moves by 6 bytes (the chunk hashes in its import paths) and its row reads 169.8 as before. Most of it is `figuresEs`: the abbreviations as keys cost about 340 bytes over a plain array in figure order, kept because D-832 names the shape. `landmark.ts` and the name readers add nothing yet: nothing in a chunk imports them until the scene's task does, which spends the other ≤ 1 KB.
- **D-820 — The field has two homes: the hand camera's `fovDeg`, and the window's own state under the sensor.** (R125; FR-SKY-14, FR-WIN-1, FR-GUT-3, FR-STAR-4 as amended; D-798.) `HandState` gains `fovDeg`, held in [`WINDOW_FOV_MIN_DEG`, `WINDOW_FOV_MAX_DEG`] by `clampWindowFov` beside the constants in `projection.ts`; `zoomBy(state, factor)` and `resetZoom(state)` are the reducers, `zoomBy` / `resetZoom` the store's moves, and every other move keeps the field, so picking a point keeps the zoom. `createHandCamera` takes a `HandAim` (the field optional, `WINDOW_FOV` unless given), `handRotation` takes the aim alone (a field is no part of a rotation), and `facePeak` and `facingOf` on the store default to the state's own field, so FR-SKY-7's tilt is reckoned at the current zoom. The store remembers the field the peak was last faced at (`peakFovDeg`), and the picker compares the peak at that field, so a zoom — which moves no aim — leaves `peak` pressed. The hand camera's field is page state: the chart's slot keeps it through the dome and back as it keeps the facing (FR-SKY-14: only `0`, the range's ends and a reload change it), and every page opens at `WINDOW_FOV`. `clampWindowFov` snaps a field within 1e-9° of `WINDOW_FOV` to it, so a zoom in and back out names no field. D-798 wrote "the screen's sensor state gains `fovDeg`": the sensor camera carries no state (`SENSOR_CAMERA` is one value), so under it the field is `SkyWindow`'s own `useState(WINDOW_FOV)`, written by the pinch alone — every mount, so every opening of the screen, starts at the default and `SkyScreen.tsx` needed nothing. `useViewRotation` returns the hand's state beside the rotation, and the window's `fovDeg` is the hand's or the sensor's; `View.fovDeg` carries it to the projection, the placeholder, the ground state and the bracket, which was already a function of `view` (FR-GUT-3's "no new constant" held). `ZOOM_WHEEL_RATE` and `ZOOM_KEY_FACTOR` are `camera.ts`'s, beside the dome's three the hand imports. The stars page's `In this field` builds its view from the deferred camera's field, so the list follows a zoom as it follows a drag.
- **D-821 — One pointer handler on every box: the second pointer ends the drag and makes the pinch; the finger left after it does not drag.** (R125; FR-SKY-14, FR-STAR-4 as amended; D-798, D-750.) `SkyWindow` keeps a map of the active pointers. One pointer is FR-STAR-4's drag, under the hand only; the second makes the two a pinch — the drag ends where it is and its pending move is dropped, so the picture does not jump as the second finger lands — and a third is nothing. This supersedes R113's "a second pointer while the first is down is ignored, and so is its lift" (`SkyWindow.test.tsx`'s case is rewritten). The pinch's factor is the product of the two pointers' distance before over after since the last frame (fingers apart narrow the field), multiplied into one pending factor that ctrl + wheel and the keys share, and applied in the drag's animation frame: one zoom per frame whatever drove it, about the centre, the aim untouched. When one finger lifts the pinch is over and the finger left does not take up the drag: a jump to where it now stands would be the first thing the reader saw; a new finger drags again. The pointer handlers are on every box, the sensor's too (the screen's pinch), and `touch-action: none` moves from the hand's class to `.box` so the browser's own pinch is off over the notes as well as the drawing; `tabIndex`, the keys and `data-dragging` stay the hand's. The `wheel` listener is native and `passive: false` — React registers `wheel` passive, and a passive listener cannot keep the browser from zooming the page — calling `preventDefault` only with `ctrlKey`; `+`/`=`/`-`/`0` with ctrl or meta are left to the browser (FR-SKY-14: the browser's own ctrl + `+` untouched), and the arrows turn with any modifier as before. A pointer is forgotten when it leaves the box uncaptured and when a new primary pointer of its type lands (every earlier one has lifted), so a capture that failed cannot leave a ghost finger that makes the next touch a pinch; two fingers that land on one point pinch from where they first part. The hover's label stays the hand's. The drag's 4 px per degree is the dome's at every field, so a 20° field drags more of itself per pixel; that is what "zoom changes the projection's scale and nothing else" means for the hand.
- **D-822 — The readout's suffix is drawn from R123's word, read either side of it; `data-fov` is the tests' handle.** (R125; FR-SKY-14; D-798, D-791, §16.23.) The ` · field 30°` / ` · campo 30°` suffix needs the word, which the task list makes R123's ("every string of the phase", the live lane, in this task's wave), and no two tasks of a wave name one file, so R125 adds no string. `SkyWindow` reads `t.window.field` through a typed optional field (`{ readout: unknown; field?: string }`), so a key R123 gives another type is a type error — as `screen` was read either side of R62 — and draws ` · ${word} ${degrees}` (rounded to 5°) while the field is not `WINDOW_FOV` and the word is a string; without it the readout is the one line. The assumption recorded: R123's key is `window.field`, the bare word (`field` / `campo`), as the task entry names it. The window's root carries `data-fov` in whole degrees, which `window-zoom.spec.ts` and `sky-screen.spec.ts` read; the readout's first line is held to its shape with the suffix optional, and the next window task after R123 (R127) tightens it to ` · field 30°`. `SkyWindow.test.tsx` exercises the suffix path by putting the word on the catalog for one test, so the composition is covered before R123 lands. *(R123, on merging R125)* R123's key is `window.field`, but a function of the degrees that carries its separator (` · field 30°` / ` · campo 30°`), as `following` takes the key, so the word order is the catalog's in each language; `SkyWindow` calls it directly, the optional read and the test's catalog patch are gone, and `SkyWindow.test.tsx` checks the suffix in both languages.
- **D-823 — One screen by the passes the page hands it; the chart's `inventory` means "no pass in the scene".** (R126; FR-SKY-6, FR-FSC-1 as amended v2.5, FR-GUT-4..6; D-794, D-783.) D-794 has the gutter's ticks and chip read the scene's passes. `SkyScene` carries only the stars, and the window already draws a tick for every pass it is handed, so the passes stay a prop beside the scene and `gutter.ts` is unchanged. `SkyScreen`'s stars inventory takes an optional `passes`: the stars page hands them whenever `[ passes ]` is on (an empty set too — a night with nothing to name is still the live page's screen, with FR-GUT-6's empty-sky chip) and none with it off. The screen tells `SkyChart` `inventory: 'stars'` only where it was handed none, so the chart's prop now means "the scene carries no pass" (no tick, no chip, no legend, no next-event block, D-783); the screen's own `data-inventory` still names the page that opened it, and the page's `onClose` is the way back. The highlight stays `null` and the colours the series', as on the live page. The stars page's own window takes the same passes with `colorBy: 'pass'` and the legend's keys (`legendKeys(legendRows(…))`, as `SkyChart` derives them), so the keys at the peaks agree between the page, its list and the screen.
- **D-824 — `[ passes ]` is a third layers row, and the set is the live page's, rebuilt in the `stars` chunk.** (R126; FR-SKY-6, FR-STAR-3, FR-COMP-4; D-776, D-794.) The two rows of two stay as D-776 counted them, and `[x] passes` / `[x] pases` (10 and 8 cells) stands alone under them on every width; one more on the second row would be 33 cells in English and 34 in Spanish, inside 36 but tighter than any other row of the page for no gain. The toggle is `useState(false)` in `StarsSky`, so it is off on every open and never reaches the prefs. The passes are the store's run once it is in for this page's place (`passesRunIn`: `sameLocation`, and finished or standing in with passes, the live page's `liveState` rule); until then the screen is handed none and stays the stars inventory, so no chip says "nothing tonight" for a night not yet computed. The set is the live page's own: `LIVE_WINDOW_MS` and `livePasses` move from `Live.tsx` to `src/lib/livePasses.ts`, which both pages import, so the `stars` chunk takes them without the live chunk, and the arcs' states are `liveArcs.ts`'s `arcKey` / `withArcStates`. The page's now is its 10 s tick; the array is remade only when the set or an arc's state changes, and the legend's rows are worked out once per tick in `StarsSky` for the window's keys and the list.
- **D-825 — A pass's row in `In this field` is the list's four columns and not a control.** (R126; FR-SKY-6, FR-STAR-7, FR-STAR-10 as amended v2.5, FR-LEG-3; D-794, D-832.) `fieldPasses` lists, in the legend's order and with its keys and series colours, every pass any part of whose drawn arc is in the box — the part flown so far while it is up (`cutTrack`), the whole track before and after, resampled at the window's 2° step and tested segment by segment against the box, so an arc that crosses a zoomed-in field between two samples is listed — ahead of the stars and inside `FIELD_LIST_MAX`: the passes first, the brightest objects in what is left, so FR-STAR-7's list stays at twelve rows (`fieldRows`). A row's state is one of FR-LEG-3's three words; a pass with none (`'full'`) is not listed. The row is the stars' grid: the key, the two-cell swatch and the name in the cut name column; the legend's FR-LEG-3 word (`up` / `soon` / `gone`) in the magnitude's column; the peak's altitude; its 16-point direction. A pass has no star label to name, so the row is not a button; its text is `aria-hidden` and one visually hidden sentence ("A: ISS (ZARYA) · up · peaks 64° up · NNW") is what is read, so a cut name is whole there. The list's star names go through `starName(catalog, i, lang)` with the page's language (`fieldObjects` takes `lang`); the window's drawn names are R127's.
- **D-832 — The Spanish names are the catalogue's data, built from one committed list and picked by language.** (FR-STAR-1, FR-STAR-6, FR-STAR-10, FR-SKY-10, FR-SKY-11, FR-SKY-12 as amended v2.5; V25-16, amending D-748's "the same in both languages".) Numbered after the task blocks because it came after they were reserved (§16.23). `scripts/build-stars.ts` reads `data-src/stars/names-es.tsv` (tab-separated, `#` comments; `con` rows by IAU abbreviation and part, `all` for Serpens whole; `star` rows keyed by the IAU name the catalogue carries) and writes into `catalog.json` a sparse `nameEs` column (the empty string where a star has no row, so the column costs the fourteen names and the separators) and a `figuresEs` table (`Record<abbr, string[]>`, 89 part names, and `wholeEs: { Ser: 'Serpiente' }`); the build fails on a `star` key the catalogue does not carry, an abbreviation outside the 88, a missing part or a duplicate. `src/lib/skyStars.ts` gains the only three ways a name is read: `starName(i, lang)` (the Spanish name where there is one, else the IAU name, else the designation as today), `figureName(con, part, lang)` and `constellationName(con, lang)` (the whole: `Serpens` / `Serpiente`, otherwise the one part's name), so no caller indexes `name` or `CONSTELLATION_NAMES` directly from here on (`constellations.ts` keeps the English table, now read only through them). The spaced capitals take `toLocaleUpperCase(lang)` before spacing (`O R I Ó N`); the abbreviation fallback is unchanged. `tests/data/starCatalog.test.ts` gains: every one of the 88 abbreviations and 89 parts has a Spanish name; every `nameEs` entry equals its TSV row and no non-empty entry lacks one; the fourteen star rows all resolve. `controlRows.test.ts` gains the two longest Spanish names at 360 px in `In this field` (one line, `…`, the whole name as accessible name). The `stars` row grows by about 0.7 KB gzipped against FR-SKY-10's added ≤ 1 KB; `main` does not move. The name list is the owner's to review on the PR; a session changes it only on the owner's word.
- **D-802 — The scene hook takes its stars from a source the page hands it.** (FR-SKY-1, FR-SKY-8, FR-SKY-10; D-788, D-791; R119.) `useSkyScene({ observer, now, starsLayer, source })` builds the scene in one `useMemo` on `(lat, lon, now, starsLayer, source.catalog, source.positionsAt)` — the source's fields, not the object, so a page may build it inline, with FR-STAR-3's four switches all on under the one toggle — the table, not the switches, keeps the figures and the names off the polar chart and the dome. `source` is `{ catalog, positionsAt }`: the catalogue in the scene's shape and `starsAt`, which R123's loader supplies once the `stars` chunk is in and `null` before; so the hook imports neither the catalogue nor `lib/skyStars.ts`, and `astronomy-engine` stays out of whatever chunk a page that calls it sits in. D-788's fourth key, `sunAltDeg`, arrives with the twilight step that reads it (R123, D-791): a key nothing reads would misstate what the memo depends on. Without a source, with the toggle off or without an instant the hook returns one shared `{ stars: null }`, so a view's memo on the scene holds across ticks that change nothing.
- **D-803 — A view reads the scene through `sceneFor`, and the polar chart and the dome place anchors before they draw.** (FR-SKY-1; D-788, D-792, D-793; R119.) `layers.ts`'s `sceneFor(view, scene)` applies the table: the switches the view does not draw go off, the stars are cut to the view's cap (a prefix through the last star at the cap, cut once per catalogue and cap; in D-748's magnitude order that is exactly the stars at the cap, and `starsFor` holds the cap star by star whatever the order), a view that draws no figures carries none; a scene the table leaves whole — the window's today — comes back as the same object. `starsFor(view, field)` is the one placement rule the polar chart and the dome share: each star at the cap above the horizon, then each planet above it. R119 draws no star, but the three views already read the scene: the window through `sceneFor` where it read `props.scene`; the polar chart mounts one empty `<g data-star|data-planet transform>` per star above the horizon and per planet, under the grid where R122's glyphs go; the dome one `GlyphHotspot` each on the unit sphere (`domeLayers.starAnchors`, `DomeLayers.anchors`), a span with `data-star` or `data-planet` and no text, where R124's points go under it. No pixel changes — an empty group and an empty hotspot paint nothing — and the anchors are what the contract test's star case reads today, as it reads the compass names (D-56). The dome's anchor span carries no `data-side`: that attribute marks the spans a view writes text into, and the contract's allowed-text rule reads them.
- **D-804 — The star case checks each view against its own projection, within its own tolerance.** (FR-SKY-1, US-41 AC3; §9.7; R119.) The case mounts each view with a scene of one star (az 120°, alt 40°) and one planet (Venus, az 150°, alt 25°) and a facing of 135° at a 35° tilt — a hand camera for the window, `initialFacingAzDeg` for the dome — so both bodies are in the window's field. Each view must carry exactly one `data-star="0"` and one `data-planet="Venus"` inside its drawing, no figure, and a name only in the window (the table's `names` row). Then: the polar chart's `translate` against `toPolar × HORIZON_R` in the store's convention, within 0.01 user units (it writes two decimals); the window's `x`/`y` against `project(uprightRotation(135, 35), …)` in the viewBox's box, within half a pixel; the dome's hotspot overlay (glyphcss writes `left`/`top` in px) against the dome's own `projectToScreen` at the facing and tilt the root reports, through an affine map fitted from three of FR-DOME-4's degree numbers — fixed anchors that never move — and checked on the fourth, within one cell of the line layer. The three views' anchors are compared across views at the end, as the legend orders are.
- **D-808 — Where D-789 and D-790 landed in the code.** (R121; FR-SKY-2, FR-SKY-7, FR-WIN-5 as amended v2.5.) Four readings the two decisions left open. *The load guard is the prefs slice's, not `localPrefs.ts`'s:* `createPrefsSlice` asks `deps.wide` once at load (`viewportIsWide`, `lib/layout.ts`'s `WIDE_QUERY`) and reads a stored `window` as the dome below the breakpoint **without rewriting it** — `localPrefs.ts` may not import the breakpoint (PLAN §3), and a narrowing read there would be written back by the next write-through of any other preference on a phone-sized window, costing the desk reader the view they chose; the layer round-trips all three values and `model/prefs.ts`'s `savedChartView` becomes `compactChartView`. *`facePeak(peak, fovDeg)` takes no state:* the peak decides both numbers, and the drop below the centre is `min(15°, fovDeg / 4)` so a narrowed field (D-798) still holds the peak. *The compact choice without a sensor (`handWindow`) and the hand camera's one `HandSlot` are `useChartHand`'s*, held by the page as D-789 says — the live page holds them (`SkyChart`'s `chartHand`), since it mounts one chart for the landscape rail, another for portrait and none while the sky screen is up; the pass detail's chart, which stays mounted under its screen, holds its own — and the slot is filled by the window in its own chunk, so the dome and back, a rotation and a trip to the screen keep the facing; the choice is dropped the moment the layout is wide, so the saved view is what comes back. *The guide's box takes the shape as a ratio:* the pass detail's frame is not aspect-locked — its box is the square the stylesheet caps at `--chart-size` — so `ChartFrame` writes `--chart-box-aspect` from the viewport on every browser resize and the stylesheet puts it on the box's `aspect-ratio`; the live page's `fill` frame takes `windowBox` inside its measurement. A ratio, not a length, so no px lands in a wide block (`breakpoint.test.ts`).
- **D-809 — The facing picker is the window lane's, and its option list is its page's.** (R121; FR-SKY-7, FR-STAR-4; D-790.) `window/FacingPicker.tsx` moves from the stars page; the lists `FACING_OPTIONS` (the eight points, `up`) and `PEAK_FACING_OPTIONS` (`peak` first) live in `SkyChart.types.ts`, so a page in the main chunk names one without pulling the window's chunk, and `camera.ts` re-exports them with `facingOf(state, peak)`, the one pressed-option rule: `up` at the top of the tilt range, `peak` where the hand is exactly where `facePeak` put it, a point the hand is exactly at, nothing after a drag. On the chart the picker stands in the rail on wide (the frame's `aside`) and in the controls row on compact; the readout is the frame's `status` slot, moved to the box's top-left corner on wide and left in its row on compact; the hand hint (`window.handHint`, the dome's words) stands in the box's bottom-left on both, where the horizon's name may cross it at a low tilt — secondary copy, left as D-789 placed it.
- **D-810 — What the window in the box measures, and what the third option costs the mid widths.** (R121; FR-SKY-2, FR-FSC-6 as amended v2.5, FR-SKY-9, FR-DS-3; D-702, D-799.) The box, cut to the viewport's shape: the live page's 798 × 498 px at 1280 × 800 and 1438 × 809 at 1920 × 1080 (the rail's complement at the viewport's ratio), the pass detail's 424 × 265 at 1280 × 800 (the guide's 44-cell square at the same ratio). The set re-shot on this machine against a same-machine `7d41477` build: 158 files byte-identical, 116 moved, all by the task's named moves — the view row's third option (a 93 × 16 px box in English, 102 × 16 in Spanish, the readout beside it shifted right by as much on wide), the screen's placeholder facing the peak at `facePeak`'s tilt (`v1-window-844-*`, 33° for a 48° peak where D-241's rule gave 26°), and one wart: at the live page's mid widths — 1024 and 1200 px, and the scrubbing page's chart column at 1280 — the toggle with `[ ] Window` (35 cells, 37 in Spanish) no longer fits beside the dome's readout, so its third option wraps alone under the first two and the dome stands one row lower. Two levers were tried and reverted: `flex-wrap: nowrap` on the toggle makes the grid's `auto` column take the whole toggle and the readout wraps or clips instead; a container rule cannot help, because the frame's shell measures the box *and the rail* (over 100 cells at 1024), and a threshold on the box column alone would be a second `@container` condition under FR-DS-3 — a `lib/layout.ts` constant, the listing and `breakpoint.test.ts`'s "one container query" — which is a design change for the owner, not this task's. And it is not a wart only: the fold table (`foldRows`, D-448) and the shape matrix count the controls row as one line, so the wrap moves the fold a row earlier at 1200 × 450 and puts the 740 × 360 box 4 px under its floor — six e2e failures, and the task is blocked on the owner's choice (`sdd-run/R121.blocked.md`: the readout into the box's corner on the wide live page as the window's is, a second container threshold under FR-DS-3, or shorter options).
- **D-811 — The polar chart's glyphs take the window's ink offsets.** (FR-SKY-4, FR-STAR-6 as amended, FR-SKY-10; D-752, D-792; R122.) Each glyph is centred by `text-anchor: middle` and `dominant-baseline: central` and shifted by `inkOffsets.ts`'s `dx`/`dy` for its glyph and size, as in the window, so a `.`'s ink and not its em box sits on its point (box-centred, a `.` lands about 2 user units, some 1.8° of sky, below it). The offsets are px at the token's size, and a chart text token on SVG text is that many user units (D-812), so they apply unscaled. The group renders once more when `inkOffsetsReady()` lands, as the window's nodes are written once more. The first cut left the offsets out to keep `main` inside FR-SKY-10 (0.9 KB without them, 1.3 KB with); D-813's chunk takes that cost out of `main` altogether, so the reason went with it.
- **D-812 — "Scaled by the chart's unit as its labels are" means the sheet's chart text tokens set on SVG text.** (FR-SKY-4; D-792; R122.) The compass labels are a CSS `font-size` on SVG `<text>`, which is a length in the 250-unit viewBox's user units, so they scale with the box. The star glyphs do the same: `font-size: var(--chart-text-18 | 15 | 12)` from `starGlyphs.ts`'s ladder, so a 12 px rung is 12 user units, the cardinals' size. The collision rule runs on the projected points in those units at `COLLISION_PX` (6), the planets ranked by their magnitude with the stars, so of a close pair the brighter is drawn, whichever kind it is.
- **D-813 — The polar chart's star group is its own lazy chunk, on the window's sheet and draw order.** (FR-SKY-4, FR-SKY-10, FR-STAR-6; D-791, D-792, D-811; R122.) `polar/PolarStars.tsx` holds the group and `SkyPolar.tsx` loads it with `React.lazy` under a `Suspense` with no fallback: the group has nothing to draw until the page's `stars` chunk has given the scene its stars, so it loads beside that one, and `starGlyphs.ts`, `inkOffsets.ts` and `layers.ts` land in a chunk shared with the window and the dome instead of `main` — measured on the build, `main` is 170.0 KB against the parent's 170.6, where D-792 expected `starGlyphs.ts` charged to `main`. The two views share three things that were copies: `starGlyphs.module.css`, one sheet keyed by `data-size` and `data-tone` (the rung's own token names), so no view keeps a class map another can miss; `magnitudeOrder`, the collision walk's order in `starGlyphs.ts` (stable, a missing or NaN magnitude last, as `rungFor` puts it on the faintest rung); and the magnitude on `starsFor`'s `PlacedBody`. The window's picture is unchanged. The placement is memoised on the scene's parts — the catalogue, the positions (one object per instant, D-791), the two switches, the orientation — so a scene rebuilt around the same positions neither places nor renders the group again. `SkyPolar.live.svg` is built from a scene written by hand, so neither a catalogue edit nor an `astronomy-engine` patch rewrites the chart's geometry snapshot; the real catalogue keeps a test of its own.
- **D-814 — `[ stars ]` on compact is the view row's second text line, not the readout row.** (FR-SKY-3, FR-COMP-4, FR-COMP-5, FR-COMP-7; D-791, D-834; R123.) FR-SKY-3 puts the toggle on the live page's actions row and the pass detail's view row within FR-COMP-4; the compact actions rows hold 32 to 34 of their 34 cells (FR-COMP-7), so on the compact live page it goes past the view to the chart as R78's bar did (D-449): `ChartFrameSlots` gains `viewAction`, which `SkyChart` puts after the view control wherever it places the control, and `readoutAction`, which the frame puts at the end of the status row where that row is its own (never in the box's corner, D-834, nor on a screen, FR-FSC-1). D-791 read "compact: the readout row"; built that way it was measured and failed: the dome's readout fits beside `[x] stars` at one facing and not at the next and Spanish never does, so the row takes a second text row and the box pays it — 373 px against FR-COMP-5's 374 at 390 × 844 scrubbing, 282 against `COMPACT_BOX_MIN_SHORT_PX` 304 at 390 × 667, the watching box 306 against D-480's 329 — and on the guide the polar chart's convention line wrapped to three rows beside it, so the polar frame no longer matched the dome's (`sky-dome.spec.ts`). The view row costs nothing: on compact its options are `inline` in one 48 px tap row (R121, D-834), the control is 33 cells, and the toggle, `inline` too, wraps to the row's second text line inside the same 48 px. Its tap box reaches down from its own line only (`SkyChart.module.css`, `.viewRow`), standing over the options' boxes there: `inline-control`'s box, a quarter row above and below, covered the options on the line above, and a tap on `Polar` landed on the toggle. So on compact portrait, on both pages, the toggle is the view row's second line (`viewAction`); on the landscape phone, whose narrow column already wraps the control to two lines at 740 × 360, it ends the readout row (`readoutAction`), held at two text rows so a readout that wraps beside it at one facing and not the next never moves the box, which `shapes.spec.ts` holds over `LIVE_BOX_MIN_PX`. Wide: the live page's actions row in both states, the pass detail's view row. The toggle is `OptionToggle` standing alone, named "Stars under the arcs" / "Estrellas bajo los arcos", so the visible word starts its name. With it on the wide actions row, `shapes.spec.ts`'s `[ see this pass ]` table moves: the English short wide rows (1200 × 450, 1400 × 480, 1920 × 500) now hold the control on the path, and 964 × 420 and 1024 × 450 in Spanish carry it on a second actions line.
- **D-815 — The twilight step cuts the scene's catalogue, and the source carries the steps.** (FR-STAR-13, FR-SKY-3, FR-SKY-10; D-788, D-791, D-802, D-806; R123.) `useSkyScene` may not import `skyStars.ts` (`astronomy-engine`, D-802), so `StarSource` gains `drawnRungs` and `drawnMagLimit` beside `positionsAt`; the source is `screens/stars/source.ts`, re-exported by `Stars.tsx` so the chunk keeps its one entry and `starsChunk.ts` its one request. The Sun's altitude is the positions' own: `starsAt` evaluates it with the planets at the same instant (`StarsAt.sunAltDeg`), so the step follows the shown `t` exactly — the live page's bodies are throttled to once a wall second (FR-LIVE-5), which at 3600× is an hour of sky, and a step read from them let a scrub into the day draw a night sky. With every rung drawn the scene is the whole field; with fewer the catalogue is cut to `drawnMagLimit` — a prefix, in D-748's magnitude order, by `catalogCut.ts`'s `cutCatalog`, the one copy the views' caps (`layers.ts`) use too, in a module of its own so `main`, which carries the hook for the pass detail, takes the cut and not the layer table — once per catalogue and limit, the positions stay whole (every view counts its stars by the catalogue's length) and the figures are left out, since their lines would run to stars the step hides; with none the scene is the shared `{ stars: null }`. The planets go with the first two rungs (`planetsDrawn` is true wherever a rung is drawn), so the scene needs no planet switch for the step and the source does not carry `planetsDrawn`. The scene's names layer is off: the pass pages do not offer it (FR-SKY-3, OQ-45), and a tap names a star apart from it (FR-STAR-7). The pass detail holds its drawing's instant while its sheet is `inert` behind another layer, so nothing unseen is placed again each second; a failed `stars` chunk is asked for again on `online` or after 30 s; and with the toggle off the idle prefetch fetches the module and builds no catalogue. The stars page builds its own scene (`Stars.tsx`, R115) and is not moved onto the hook here: `Stars.tsx` is R125's file in this wave, so its twilight step is left to R126, which holds the page's list in the next.
- **D-816 — The pass detail evaluates its bodies once, the loader is shared, and `main` pays for the pass detail.** (FR-SKY-3, FR-SKY-8, FR-SKY-10; D-149, D-545, D-791; R123.) The pass detail's instant is its own `now`, ticking (FR-FSC-8); the page evaluates the Sun and the Moon there through `useSkyBodies` for the scene's step and hands both to the chart and the screen, which would otherwise each evaluate them again. `useStarSource` (`components/live`) asks for the `stars` chunk when the page mounts with the toggle on, and with it off prefetches it through `whenIdle`, the settings page's idle rule now one helper for both (`screens/whenIdle.ts`); the source is kept at module level, so a second pass detail draws its stars from its first frame. The passes screen takes the page's scene (`SkyScreen`'s passes inventory gains `scene`). Because the pass detail is in `main`, the scene hook, the loader, the toggle and the slots land there, with the phase's strings: `main` grows by 1.2 KB over the parent, past FR-SKY-10's ≤ 1 KB for the phase; the overrun is accepted for the release's D-178 re-set, and the numbers are in R123's Done note. `live-perf.spec.ts` enters scrubbing before it picks 3600×: since v2.0 the speeds are the scrubbing state's (FR-WATCH-1), and the spec had not run since.
- **D-817 — The drag rate is the best of three drags, and the constant is the middle of three runs.** (FR-SKY-5, FR-GUIDE-6; D-62, D-793; R124.) On one build and one page, three 5 s drags under the 6× throttle read 39.4, 46.5 and 56.6/s — a swing twice the tenth FR-SKY-5 allows — and every swing is downward: another process taking the core slows the page, and nothing speeds it up. So `dome-perf.spec.ts` drags three times on the same page and reports the best drag as the rate the page can do; a median would have failed an honest build one run in three (46.5 against a floor of 52.0), where the best of three varied within 1/s across runs (59.8, 59.4, 58.8). The committed constant is the middle of three such runs on `ece8bfd` (390 px 59.4, 1280 px 53.1, Apple silicon, 2026-10-26); the floor is nine tenths of the phone's and never under 30, and the desktop's is reported, not gated (D-91). The log line carries the line layer's braille dot count, so a run says whether the stars were on (1132 without, 1154 with the twenty and five). The constant is one machine's, as D-62's numbers are, and the spec stays a measurement run with `DOME_PERF=1`, never a CI gate; on another machine the runner measures `ece8bfd` by the same spec and hands the phone's rate in as `DOME_PERF_ECE8BFD`, which replaces the constant for that run.
- **D-818 — The point mark is a two-vertex polygon at one place.** (FR-SKY-5; D-793; R124.) glyphcss's wireframe pass skips a polygon with fewer than two vertices, keeps one edge per pair of endpoints (so three vertices at one place are the same single edge again), and its braille line routine plots exactly the sub-cell a zero-length edge falls in; the hidden-line depth pass skips polygons under three vertices, so the mark costs nothing there. A dot that lands on a set dot — a ring, a meridian, the horizon, the meridians' crowd near the zenith — adds nothing to the raster, which is the reading, not a defect: the snapshot's bodies are placed off the grid so the raster test can count five.
- **D-819 — Measured before R123 with a field handed to a scratch build; the desktop's cost reported, not fixed.** (FR-SKY-5, US-40 AC4; D-793, D-791; R124.) R123 wires the stars into the live page in the same wave, so this branch's page hands the dome no scene and the committed spec measures the stars only once R123 merges. The task's measure came from a build of this branch under `node_modules/.cache/` with twenty stars at the cap and five planets handed to the dome when the page hands none (`sdd-run/r124-build.cjs`, untracked): 390 px 57.2/s (−3.7 % of 59.4), 1280 px 43.9/s (−17 % of 53.1). The phone holds, which is the gate. The desktop's loss was isolated and not explained: the hotspots alone cost nothing (55.5/s at 1280), the colour about 3/s, and a real tiny triangle in place of the degenerate polygon costs the same, so what remains is a per-polygon cost in glyphcss's per-frame scene assembly that twenty-five polygons make visible at 65 columns. The cap is the spec's (D-793), so the dots stay; whether to chase that cost (passing the dots as `wireframe` edges instead of polygons is the first thing to try) is a follow-up for the owner. So the spec's FR-GUIDE-6 test measures the pass detail's dome as the page hands it, and its FR-SKY-5 test (the floor) runs only on a dome that carries star anchors and is skipped until R123 hands it a scene, rather than passing on a dome without the stars.
- **D-826 — The landmark is picked at the peak's own instant, the names ride on the scene, and the pass detail asks for the stars source whatever the toggle says.** (R127; FR-SKY-11, FR-SKY-12, FR-STAR-10 as amended; D-796, D-802, D-832.) Three readings D-796 left open. *The instant:* FR-SKY-11 wants the landmark "computed once per instant with the rotation" and moving "with a scrub only when the highlighted pass changes"; a peak is a fixed point of the sky over which the stars drift a degree every four minutes, so a star picked at the shown instant changed under a scrub while the pass did not (Bariloche's Tiangong pass read `Bellatrix` on the live page at its peak and `Aldebarán` on its detail five minutes before). the source places the stars once more at `pass.peak.t` — `starScene.ts`'s `sceneAt(observer, t, pass)`, kept per pass in the chunk (D-837 moved the scene there), so never per tick — and picks the landmark and the figure among them; the twilight step is the shown instant's, the drawing's, so a star the step hides now is no landmark and leaves no line — nor does a farther star the step still draws stand in for it (the full night's landmark or none) (not the figure's "passes through" either). The column (FR-SKY-12) is at each point's own instant by the same rule, computed once per pass. *The source carries the closures:* `StarParts` (`starScene.ts`) gains `landmark(positions, peak, rungs)`, `constellationAt(point, positions)` and `names: { star, figure, constellation }` closed over the reader's catalogue in the `stars` chunk, and `StarSource` hands the pages `catalog`, `positionsAt`, `constellationAt` and `names` beside `sceneAt`, so the hook, the live page and the pass detail word the line and the column without importing `lib/landmark.ts`, `lib/skyStars.ts` or the catalogue; the scene's `StarCatalog` gains the names' columns (`nameEs`, `figureNames`, `wholeNames`, optional so a hand-built catalogue reads in English) and the window reads them through `catalogNames()` and D-832's accessors, which it already reached through `stars/field.ts`. *The source on the pass detail:* `useStarSource(true)` — the `Among` column is about the fixed sky and not about the drawing, so it stands with `[ stars ]` off; the scene still reads the toggle and the drawing is unchanged. `SkyScene.landmark` is optional (absent is none), so the many hand-built scenes stand. The line is `lib/landmarkLine.ts` as D-796 says, taking the two sentences as `t.live` carries them; with a star but no figure within reach it names the star's own constellation.
